cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::cdu: no dated city-wide climate-neutrality target; focus on “effective and affordable” climate policy (incl. district-heat decarbonization); reject shutting down the gas network
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::spd: climate-neutral preferably before 2045; implement the Berlin Energy Transition Act; “Out of oil and gas. Into sun, wind and other renewables”
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::gruene: goal: climate-neutral Berlin by 2040; climate check for laws and measures; enforce the Berlin Climate Protection Act — mandatory action programs if targets are missed
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::linke: climate-neutral Berlin by 2040 at latest; keep the CO2 budget anchored in the climate law; expand climate impact assessment into a climate safeguard; sector targets for energy supply, transport, buildings and the economy
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::fdp: climate-neutral, but above all cheap, reliable, and innovative; technology openness, private investment, hydrogen, geothermal energy, solar, smart heating grids
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::afd: repeal Berlin’s Climate Protection and Energy Transition Act; replace it with a Secure Energy Act focused on security of supply, affordability and reliability
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::bsw: against activism for fixed target marks; take energy plants such as coal plants offline only when enough competitive secure alternatives exist; abolish the CO2 price; keep affordable secure supply and technology openness
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::volt: turn the BEK (Berlin Energy and Climate Protection Programme 2030) measures catalogue into a real acceleration plan that closes the 2022–2026 implementation gap; annual public reporting on delivery progress
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::tierschutz: Berlin climate-neutral by 2035 at latest (non-negotiable); public administration climate-neutral by 2035; also implement the “Berlin climate-neutral by 2030” referendum; binding CO₂ budget, shadow price, heat fully renewable by 2035
cellSummaries.climate-neutrality::oedp: Berlin climate-neutral as quickly as possible, not only by 2045; coal phase-out by 2030; align with Fridays/Scientists for Future demands
cellSummaries.a100-construction::cdu: push ahead with A100 continuation and support federal planning of the 17th section; keep cars as an indispensable part of mobility
cellSummaries.a100-construction::spd: instead of continuing A100 — repair streets and bridges, sustainable transport; A100 should end at Treptower Park
cellSummaries.a100-construction::gruene: reject further A100 construction (17th section); close the 16th section until a traffic concept exists; reject the planned four-lane TVO in its current form
cellSummaries.a100-construction::linke: A100 should end at Treptower Park; remove the 17th section from the land-use plan and push for removal from federal law
cellSummaries.a100-construction::fdp: for rapid construction of the A100 via the 17th section to Storkower Straße
cellSummaries.a100-construction::afd: for the 17th section A100 and closing the inner motorway ring
cellSummaries.a100-construction::bsw: for continuing the 17th section of the A100 to Storkower Straße, taking residents’ interests into account and with mandatory public participation
cellSummaries.a100-construction::tierschutz: stop further expansion of Stadtautobahn A100 and high-capacity roads such as TVO; outdated traffic forecasts, exploding costs, and counter to the transport transition (Verkehrswende) — fund climate-just mobility instead
cellSummaries.road-construction::cdu: Tempo 50 as the rule on main roads; invest over €200 million in bridges in 2026/27; push A100 and build the eastern tangential road (TVO)
cellSummaries.road-construction::spd: road network remains central for buses, emergency services, fire brigade, city cleaning and business traffic; instead of continuing A100, maintain streets and bridges and sustainable mobility; build the eastern tangential link (Tangentialverbindung Ost) as a road without blocking a later parallel S-Bahn
cellSummaries.road-construction::gruene: streets safer and fairer (Tempo 30, traffic calming, safe school routes); repair crumbling bridges/roads; no new motorways such as A100 — prefer retrofit over new motorways
cellSummaries.road-construction::linke: against new motorways; emphasis on repairing roads and bridges, coordinating construction sites, in conflicts, priority for the environmental transport network; new road plans only where they serve the public good
cellSummaries.road-construction::fdp: expand the road network: A100 to Storkower Straße, complete TVO, new roads in the northeast and south; Tempo 50 on important arterial roads; central coordination of construction sites
cellSummaries.road-construction::afd: A100 17th section; improve traffic flow on arterial roads instead of neighborhood traffic-calming blocks; monitoring the condition and needs of roads/parking; underground transport solutions
cellSummaries.road-construction::bsw: relieve bottlenecks in Berlin’s road network; finish A100 to Storkower Straße; expand TVO and coordinate major road/rail worksites faster
cellSummaries.road-construction::volt: Vision Zero / safer intersections and Tempo 30; end worksite chaos so road and sidewalk works disrupt traffic only while work is actually happening
cellSummaries.road-construction::tierschutz: against new major roads for private car traffic (incl. A100 and TVO); fund climate-just mobility instead
cellSummaries.road-construction::oedp: give priority to mobility projects by environmental and public benefit; less car traffic
cellSummaries.new-u-bahn-construction-line-extensions:: push extensions of U2, U3, U6, U7, U8 and U9; secure planning for U10; partial CBTC automation; denser S-Bahn to outer districts; advance i2030 rail with Brandenburg
continue U3 to Mexikoplatz, U7 to BER and Heerstraße, U8 to Märkisches Viertel; start planning U-Bahn Alexanderplatz–Hohenschönhausen
close gaps in the rail network; check which U-Bahn extensions/new builds are feasible by cost-benefit, ridership gains and network links
fully use the option for 1,500 U-Bahn cars and denser headways; expand the U-Bahn network mainly to close existing network gaps; extend the tram network into the west of the city
annually build 1–2 km of U-Bahn; priority U8 to Märkisches Viertel, U1 to Ostkreuz/Halensee, U7 to BER, U2 to Pankow Kirche, U5 to Tegel, U9 southward, new express line Alexanderplatz—Marzahn
rapid expansion of the rail network (no named U-Bahn lines); CBTC for denser headways; traffic-light priority; better regional-rail integration; staffing drive for BVG/S-Bahn
targeted expansion of U‑Bahn, S‑Bahn, trams and buses, especially outer districts; two cable cars and integration of “Gärten der Welt” into public transport
coordinate expansion of U-Bahn, tram, S-Bahn and regional rail in an integrated early way; prioritize full U-Bahn automation for higher frequency and round-the-clock stable operation
public-transport expansion — especially U-Bahn, S-Bahn and regional rail — as the top priority among all infrastructure projects; better connect outlying districts
expand public transport including S-Bahn and regional rail into the surrounding area; denser schedules
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::cdu: improve the bike network as needed: prioritize repairing existing paths, close gaps, develop cycle highways; Bike&Ride (bike boxes) at S-/U-Bahn stations
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::spd: cycling plan and priority cycling network, cycle highways, more bike racks, bike parking garages and Bike&Ride with lighting and weather protection; support for bike-sharing system
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::gruene: end the bike-lane freeze; protected lanes and bike streets; advance Ost/West/Wannsee cycle highways; reliable winter clearing; expand Bike&Ride parking at stations
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::linke: safe continuous network of bike lanes/streets and cycle highways per the network plan; protected lanes; expand Bike&Ride parking at stations; restore public bike-share with 30 free minutes plus a transit ticket
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::fdp: expand bike streets parallel to arterial roads; thoroughly renew the network, cycle highways, repair existing paths; where routing through quiet streets is not possible — protected bike lanes at roadway level
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::afd: expansion “in moderation”: monitoring demand, routes on neighboring/parallel side streets, markings instead of modal filters, 1 000 modular lockable bike-parking spaces
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::bsw: connected and safe cycling network, especially in outer districts; bike lanes should not end “nowhere”; safe routing, where possible physically separated from cars
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::volt: protected bike lanes, bike streets and cycle highways; build cycle highways consistently and quickly; Bike&Ride at stations
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::tierschutz: protected bike lanes on main streets, at least 365 km of new bike lanes per year, priority for cycling infrastructure over parking and car lanes
cellSummaries.cycling-infrastructure::oedp: redesign streets for more and safer cycling
cellSummaries.parking::cdu: keep parking in public space; radically simplify paid parking management; affordable resident parking; expand neighborhood garages; more Bike&Ride and charging at mobility hubs
cellSummaries.parking::spd: expand managed parking zones with Scan-Cars; higher resident-permit fees earmarked for the eco-mobility network (transit, cycling, walking) and neighborhood parking garages; after-hours supermarket/authority lots; digital parking guidance; more commercial short-stay and loading zones; upgrade Park&Ride
cellSummaries.parking::gruene: managed parking to curb non-resident all-day parking and free space for the eco-mobility network (transit, cycling, walking); raise resident parking fees (revenue shared, Land share to transit); Scan-Cars; expand craft parking permits to care workers; more reservable loading zones and micro-depots
cellSummaries.parking::linke: expand managed paid parking and enforcement through Scan Cars; SUV parking more expensive following the Paris model; redistribute parts of streets/parking areas for walking/cycling, trees and quality of public space; delivery and service-vehicle parking zones for necessary traffic
cellSummaries.parking::fdp: demand-based parking fees; do not artificially reduce parking spaces; private underground garages; Park&Ride Mobility Hubs with reservable spaces at regional/S-Bahn lines
cellSummaries.parking::afd: restore removed parking spaces; digital parking management; managed paid parking reduce to the necessary minimum; resident parking should remain cheap; expand Park&Ride on the outskirts
cellSummaries.parking::bsw: against the “unnecessary destruction of parking spaces”; parking management, neighborhood garages, loading zones and better organization of parked traffic; Park&Ride at the city edges
cellSummaries.parking::volt: Park&Ride at city borders and in outer districts; paid digital parking based on size and emissions; reducing parking spaces for sidewalks, bike lanes, and greenery
cellSummaries.parking::tierschutz: expand Park&Ride; citywide paid parking with fees by vehicle size; cycling infrastructure has legal priority over parking spaces
cellSummaries.parking::oedp: more free Park&Ride spaces on the periphery
cellSummaries.ev-charging::cdu: continue expanding charging infrastructure; reliable public charging points; charging points in Park&Ride/Bike&Ride‑hubs; hydrogen as a supplement for heavy transport, buses, and ships
cellSummaries.ev-charging::spd: continue expanding public charging; additional charging points in store parking lots, fast charging while shopping; better charging infrastructure for passenger shipping
cellSummaries.ev-charging::gruene: speed the shift to zero-emission vehicles — starting with BVG buses; stepwise zero-emission zone in line with the BEK (Berlin Energy and Climate Protection Programme 2030); zero-emission e-bus fleet — no separate pledges on public car chargers
cellSummaries.ev-charging::linke: public charging via the municipal utility, usable also by tenants without a private space; strengthen electric commercial traffic with small e-vans, e-cars and cargo bikes
cellSummaries.ev-charging::fdp: rapid, demand-driven expansion of charging points across Berlin; cut bureaucracy and ease private investment; fast-charging hubs, supermarket chargers, smart charging in public space
cellSummaries.ev-charging::volt: pilot bidirectional charging so EV owners are paid for feeding stored power back to the grid; accelerate smart meters for households with electric cars
cellSummaries.ev-charging::tierschutz: expand EV charging infrastructure and unify confusing payment options; private operators should run chargers more cooperatively; reserved fast chargers for e-taxis at taxi stands; support the shift to electric mobility while still reducing overall car traffic
cellSummaries.tempelhofer-feld-development-edge-develo: for housing on the edges of the field — “20,000 new apartments”
keep the field; no edge housing while unused building potential remains elsewhere; state-owned and cooperative housing around the airport building without entering the field
against development; “the referendum is binding”; the field is “irreplaceable”
preserve Tempelhofer Feld entirely as open land; keep the referendum law; against development and privatization; develop the airport building as a social, ecological and cultural future district
start edge development immediately without a new vote; possible special economic zone “Frei-Kiez” on part of the field
Tempelhofer Feld as a test site for agri-photovoltaics and mobile energy storage; scale what works, end what does not — not framed as housing or edge development

keep Tempelhofer Feld permanently unbuilt; respect the 2014 referendum (change only by a new vote); reject edge development for cooling/air and health; open the airport building for common-good culture, sport and education
keep Tempelhofer Feld unbuilt as public leisure and recreation space per the Berlin referendum; allow partial conversion of the airport building into apartments
cellSummaries.large-scale-tree-planting-and-or-tree-ca: increase the number of street trees to 1 million by 2040; realistic goals, district involvement and reliable funding
+70% city trees by 2040; plant empty tree pits by 2027; new sites ideally every 15 m; prioritize tree retention in planning
plant one million additional trees; BäumePlus (trees-plus) Act; planting in heat hotspots, on sealed surfaces and in dense neighborhoods; reliable care and rainwater use
street trees to 1 million by 2040 under the BäumePlus (trees-plus) law / Tree Referendum; funding for planting and care; use parking spaces where needed; strengthen green-space offices and watering
regularly plant additional street trees, ensure continuous care and watering; make it easier for neighborhood initiatives to care for trees and greenery
replace every felled tree; transparent tree balances; more care for green spaces and forests

turn the decisions of the Berlin tree petition (Berliner Baumbegehren) into real tree-planting drives: reliable budget funding, priority for new planting and care; green roofs, facades and courtyards as the rule for new builds
plant more street trees for shade and accessible places to stay
tighten Berlin’s tree-protection ordinance with binding nearby replacement planting; expand urban greenery in dense, heat-stressed and disadvantaged neighbourhoods, with secured long-term care
protect city trees, hedges and woody plants as nesting sites and habitats for animals
cellSummaries.heat-protection::cdu: implement the existing Berlin Climate Adaptation Act approach in planning; more street trees (to 1 million by 2040); expand drinking fountains
cellSummaries.heat-protection::spd: Berlin Climate Adaptation Act; more greenery and cool spaces, Mini‑Parks, water and drinking fountains; act in hot spots, where heat, noise, pollution, and social burden overlap
cellSummaries.heat-protection::gruene: climate islands with shade, water and seating in hot districts; more trees, drinking fountains and misting on heat days; annually evaluate and develop the heat action plan
cellSummaries.heat-protection::linke: socially differentiated heat-protection plan with binding measures and funding; cool rooms in every neighborhood, shade on playgrounds and splash pads; do not build on cold-air generation areas such as Tempelhofer Feld
cellSummaries.heat-protection::fdp: climate adaptation focus: urban ventilation, shading, water management, extreme-weather prep, health precautions and climate monitoring — no separate heat plan / public cooling-rooms program
cellSummaries.heat-protection::bsw: invest in street trees, facade/roof greening, open water, drinking fountains and cool rooms; more public drinking points
cellSummaries.heat-protection::volt: expand Berlin’s heat action plan (coordination, funding, science); public map of free cool rooms and drinking fountains; more street trees for shade
cellSummaries.heat-protection::tierschutz: free vegan sunscreen in busy places, more drinking fountains, shade, light-colored surfaces, greening roofs and facades, heat-protection standards for construction and renovation
cellSummaries.heat-protection::oedp: cool the city via parks, trees and summer evaporation (Verdunstung); ecological urban rainwater management with storage and drainage concepts
cellSummaries.sponge-city-rainwater-retention-unsealin: develop Berlin as a sponge city; catch, store and use rainwater; decentralized rainwater use, green roofs/facades, more storage, fewer combined-sewer discharges; protect water bodies
“sponge city” with Berlin Waterworks and the rainwater agency; disconnect more rainwater from the sewer system, infiltrate it on site and use it for greenery

keep rainwater in the city (unsealing, green roofs, rain gardens, infiltration strips, rain barrels); strong unsealing program toward net-zero sealing; preserve cool-air corridors; net-zero sealing by 2030 (no net increase in sealed surfaces)

unsealing, on-site infiltration and rainwater management; improve disconnecting surfaces from combined sewers; strengthen the rainwater agency; net-zero sealing by 2030 (no net increase in sealed surfaces)

treat rainwater as a resource and handle heavy rain as a sponge city; citywide rainwater management; decentralized capture/infiltration at buildings and in street space; rainwater-management pilot districts
separate rainwater and wastewater system; 4th treatment stage; unsealing where possible, and rainwater tanks
planning principle: rain does not go into the sewer, infiltrates, is stored or used; more unsealing and rainwater use
store rainwater on site; systematic unsealing with permeable surfaces; simplify permits for green roofs/facades and water-collection tanks
store, infiltrate and evaporate rainwater on site; mandatory rainwater concepts for new builds and renovations
innovative storage and drainage concepts; modernize/integrate systems with Berliner Wasserbetriebe; use roof rainwater to water street trees and parks; fund sponge systems with green roofs
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::cdu: prevention before recycling; expand reusable systems and avoid unnecessary packaging; circular economy in construction
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::spd: Zero-Waste approach (prevention first); packaging tax on takeaway food packaging; continue NochMall and the repair bonus; raise wood-waste recycling above 25%; more organic-waste bins and more BSR composting/sorting in Berlin
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::gruene: implement the Zero-Waste strategy; citywide tax on single-use packaging, dishes and cutlery; expand Repair-Cafés, reuse stores and sharing platforms; strengthen wood-waste recycling
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::linke: strengthen the Zero-Waste agency; expand the repair bonus and repair networks; at least one second-hand store and one neighborhood circular-economy hub per district; raise recycling quotas; phase out single-use packaging
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::fdp: barcode app to help sort packaging waste; more circular construction and recycled materials in public buildings
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::bsw: circular economy as part of Berlin’s sustainability agenda; free bulky-waste collection at least twice a year; mobile recycling stations in neighborhoods
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::volt: packaging tax to cut single-use waste and fund citywide reusable-return infrastructure; Zero-Waste education workshops; Repair-Cafés and a stronger repair bonus; no new waste incinerators
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::tierschutz: packaging tax on single-use packaging; standardized reusable and deposit systems; repair/swap cafés in every neighborhood, reuse hubs and a repair bonus; circular building; material recycling before incineration
cellSummaries.zero-waste-waste-prevention::oedp: extend deposit/take-back rules to all reusable packaging types and more non-reusable containers; promote packaging-free retail; Bundesrat initiative against problematic packaging (e.g. plastic welded to aluminium); circular economy without greenwashing
cellSummaries.bsr-waste-collection-and-infrastructure:: BSR expands cleaning in parks, playgrounds and forests; low-threshold paid BSR bulky-waste pickup (incl. evening hours); more separate bins and underground containers
BSR cleans all playgrounds now and all parks/green spaces by 2030; cleaning cycles by need; staff by waste volumes; free bulky-waste pickup twice a year; more neighborhood collection days
BSR to clean all parks and playgrounds; adapt BSR Kieztage to daily life with more weekend dates; free bulky-waste disposal once a year per household; quarterly low-threshold bulky-waste days

more recycling centers and nearby drop-offs (incl. bulky-waste spots in large estates); underground containers in new quarters; expand BSR Kieztage for bulky waste and recycling; free bulky-waste pickup twice a year; more investment in BSR facilities

all green spaces, currently cleaned by districts, transfer to BSR; free bulky-waste pickup by arrangement; BSR neighborhood collection days more often and in more locations; separate Berlin Recycling (commercial waste) from BSR and privatize it
develop existing BSR‑recycling centers; BSR should be directly authorized to act during winter ice, with less bureaucracy
BSR is responsible for cleaning sidewalks and bike lanes; regular free bulky-waste pickup at least twice a year; mobile recycling stations by district
link Berlin-Pay with the BSR “Kehrenbürger volunteer-cleanup program”; neighborhood recycling points for recyclables, hazardous waste, and bulky waste
decentralized points for bulky waste and hazardous waste; BSR neighborhood collection days at least twice a month in every district
service-oriented disposal: decentralized points for bulky waste and hazardous waste
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::cdu: fines; about 30,000 public bins by 2030; underground containers; mobile video/AI against waste hotspots
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::spd: recognize cleanup volunteering with Ehrenamtskarte and vouchers; continue and expand BSR Kehrenbürger cleanups; teach waste prevention/recycling early; more BSR sorting plants; longer hours and new BSR recycling centers in heavily burdened districts
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::gruene: BSR to clean all parks and playgrounds; keep park runners and neighborhood managers permanently; more convenient BSR neighborhood collection days (esp. weekends); free bulky-waste disposal once a year plus quarterly bulky-waste days
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::linke: more bins and cleaning in polluted areas; cleanup actions; park rangers into permanent funding; public-order offices systematically enforce mandatory offer of reusable packaging; involve neighborhood councils in cleanliness
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::fdp: more bins and more frequent collection in parks; underground containers as standard; cleaning robots; digital fill-level sensors; public-order offices give priority to illegal dumping
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::afd: 24/7 public-order offices with consistent fines; mobile cleanup teams; video at waste hotspots; enough bins; waste sheriffs / Waste-Watchers; faster removal of abandoned cars and homeless camps
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::bsw: permanent “Berlin Cleans Up” campaign with schools, clubs, and neighborhoods; district cleaning teams, response to illegal dumping within 24 hours
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::volt: more bins and separate containers for cigarette butts; multilingual information on sorting; enforcement against illegal dumping; packaging tax and reusable-packaging infrastructure
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::tierschu: more and larger bins, separate containers, dog-waste bags, “Berlin kippenfrei” (cigarette-butt free), stronger enforcement against illegal dumping
cellSummaries.cleanliness-enforcement-litter::oedp: crack down on illegal dumping, waste exports and landfills; better monitoring and sanctions; expand deposit/return and recycling procurement
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::cdu: Berlin is already a solar leader; develop PV on large and public roofs, at municipal housing companies; against mandatory solar panel installation, repeal the Berlin Solar Act
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::spd: by 2035, 25% of electricity generated in Berlin from solar via Masterplan Solarcity, SolarPlus, PV and grid-serving storage
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::gruene: all technically suitable public buildings with solar installations by 2030; strengthen SolarPLUS and Solar Center; tenant electricity from local solar installations, community PV, balcony PV with batteries; PV in parking lots and other sealed areas
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::linke: Masterplan Solarcity: 4.4 GW potential; solar installations on all suitable public-building roofs by 2030 with monitoring and consequences for non-compliance; support for balcony solar panels and tenant electricity from local solar installations
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::fdp: develop solar installations and storage, remove bureaucratic barriers; against mandatory solar on new and existing buildings
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::afd: against additional state PV retrofit mandates; weather-dependent sources cannot guarantee supply security for a metropolis
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::bsw: PV important for Berlin, but expansion only together with grids, storage, electrolyzers, power-to-heat (converting surplus electricity into heat) and reserve capacities
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::volt: solar program; all suitable public buildings with solar installations by 2031; PV in parking lots, along motorways and railways; support for tenant electricity from local solar installations and citizen projects
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::tierschutz: specific PV targets; use all suitable roofs, facades, parking lots, parking structures, noise barriers, and cycle highways; strengthen Solar Center Berlin
cellSummaries.solar-energy-photovoltaics::oedp: expansion of photovoltaics and solar installations by removing bureaucratic barriers; PV on all public-building roofs
cellSummaries.wind-energy::cdu: against large wind turbines in Berlin, especially in forests and recreation areas; at federal level reform area requirements for city-states
cellSummaries.wind-energy::spd: renewables course includes wind (“into sun, wind, and other renewables”); no separate Berlin wind-turbine siting program
cellSummaries.wind-energy::gruene: designate areas for wind; preferably commercial and industrial areas, not forests; round tables, local residents’ participation in revenues; pilots for small wind turbines on high-rises
cellSummaries.wind-energy::linke: expansion of wind energy with participation of residents and districts; implement the Wind-on-Land Act (federal rules to designate onshore wind areas); preferably industrial areas, without harming nature; districts share in profits
cellSummaries.wind-energy::fdp: make greater use of small wind turbines; surplus wind energy use through sector coupling, e.g. for heating and hydrogen
cellSummaries.wind-energy::afd: strictly reject wind turbines in Berlin, especially in forests; reject the 0.5% federal land target for wind in Berlin
cellSummaries.wind-energy::bsw: against wind turbines in Berlin; initiative to change the Wind-on-Land Act to abolish area targets; supports repowering old turbines where they already stand (replace with fewer, more powerful modern ones)
cellSummaries.wind-energy::volt: coordinate the expansion of wind and solar energy in Brandenburg with reduction of fossil energy in Berlin; use green energy without curtailing wind power
cellSummaries.wind-energy::tierschutz: put in place 8 wind-energy sites in Berlin, including Tegel, Gatow and Müggelheim; participation of residents, cooperatives, and municipal utilities in revenues
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::cdu: gas and the gas network remain important for reliable and affordable heat; against shutting down the gas network; competition between gas, district heating and heat pumps
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::spd: phase out fossil heating (“out of oil and gas”); convert the gas network toward an H₂ core network for large users; long-term GASAG buyback for climate transformation
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::gruene: gas distribution network largely not decarbonizable and in the medium/long term largely unnecessary; partial conversion to green hydrogen only for industry/commerce without alternatives; socially fair phase-out of unnecessary network sections through negotiations with GASAG
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::linke: fossil gas phase-out socially and infrastructurally coordinated; replace gas heating as quickly as possible, no longer install it in public buildings; at an appropriate price — remunicipalization/socialization of GASAG
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::fdp: no ban on exiting the gas network; defossilize heat via technology openness (hydrogen for heat, geothermal, smart grids, third-party waste heat into district heating)
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::afd: keep coal and gas power plants plus diverse import power for peak load and to prevent blackouts; technology-open baseload mix; replace the Climate Protection and Energy Transition Act (Klimaschutz- und Energiewendegesetz) with a Sichere-Energie-Gesetz — gas distribution network not addressed
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::bsw: against dismantling the gas network; support for remunicipalizing GASAG; use Nord Stream again; gas/coal do not switch off until competitive and reliable alternatives exist
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::volt: overcome gas dependence (most households and about three-quarters of district heating still on natural gas); replace fossil power/heat with renewables, (large) heat pumps and storage
cellSummaries.gas-gas-network::tierschutz: against expanding fossil gas today with a later hydrogen-swap promise (fossil lock-in); heat via renewables, heat pumps and district heating instead
cellSummaries.hydrogen::cdu: hydrogen for industry and power plants; research cluster; infrastructure along transport axes, logistics centers and industrial zones; hydrogen regional trains
cellSummaries.hydrogen::spd: build a hydrogen economy; hydrogen in individual apartments technically limited, there will be less climate-neutral gas
cellSummaries.hydrogen::gruene: green hydrogen not for heating in the foreseeable future; partial conversion of the gas network to a green-H₂ network only where industry/commercial sites cannot otherwise become climate-neutral
cellSummaries.hydrogen::linke: only green hydrogen and only where there is no direct electric alternative: ships/aviation, industry, peaks in district heating; not as mass heating
cellSummaries.hydrogen::fdp: comprehensive hydrogen strategy Berlin‑Brandenburg: production, networks, storage, large consumers; showcase‑region for hydrogen mobility and pilots for trucks, trains, ships, and cars
cellSummaries.hydrogen::bsw: expand the H₂ network only in line with demand for green hydrogen; focus use in energy-intensive industry, high-temperature processes and gas plants; invest in electrolyzers; technology openness for hydrogen and synthetic fuels
cellSummaries.hydrogen::volt: Tegel as a Green Tech Hub for hydrogen and recycling technology test fields; modular biogas plant for bio-waste that should later also run on hydrogen to cover peak demand
cellSummaries.hydrogen::tierschutz: reject hydrogen as a general heating solution; green H₂ scarce/costly and mainly needed where no electric alternative (e.g. steel, chemicals, aviation); reject fossil-gas-now/H₂-later lock-in; H₂ only where direct electrification is impossible
cellSummaries.hydrogen::oedp: notes that BEW’s announced conversion of gas power plants to “fossil-free” hydrogen by 2040 still lacks concrete, practicable implementation plans
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::cdu: heat pumps as part of competition between energy systems; use where sensible and economical; shallow and deep geothermal energy
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::spd: replace fossil heating via heat planning; promote heat pumps with storage, near-surface geothermal energy, and district/neighborhood heat
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::gruene: additional support for heat pumps, especially in single-/two-family houses and suitable apartment buildings; large heat pumps, deep geothermal energy and waste heat from data centers/wastewater
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::linke: outside heating grids, electrification is usually the most efficient; large heat pumps using river and wastewater for heating supply; geothermal energy and waste heat
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::bsw: against forcing heat pumps people cannot afford; create conditions where heat pumps make economic/technical sense — integrated into district heat with storage; support geothermal demonstration plants and research
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::volt: retrain installers from conventional heating to heat pumps; systematically convert district heating to large and river heat pumps plus waste heat from data centers, industry and U-Bahn; smart meters for heat-pump households
cellSummaries.heat-pumps::tierschutz: heat-transition fund for heat pumps, neighborhood heat, geothermal and solar thermal; PV, heat pumps, storage and smart controls as standard in municipal buildings
cellSummaries.heating-supply-networks-decarbonization-: expand and decarbonize district heating after buying Berlin’s district-heating system; Climate Pact: more than €0.5bn for district-heating build-out and decarbonization; municipal heat planning with security of supply and affordability
expand district heating via the Berlin-owned provider; network buyback enables decarbonization; BSR should take a stronger role for a climate-neutral Berlin and use waste heat

priority — decarbonize district heating before network expansion; BEW invest in large heat pumps, deep geothermal and waste heat (data centers/wastewater); against wood-fired CHP and planned waste incineration at Klingenberg

expansion of district heating and local heating grids; goal — decarbonizing heat with security of supply and affordability; heating agency, neighborhood concepts, power-to-heat (converting surplus electricity into heat), storage; do not count waste incineration as decarbonization

cut CO2 in district heating and expand central/local heating grids; allow third-party producers, e.g. waste heat from data centers and industry; sector coupling — surplus wind for heat/hydrogen; smart heating grids
end debt-financed decarbonization of Berlin’s district heating (criticizes up to €10bn); no heat-price rises from climate measures; keep fossils in the mix where needed

district heat via municipal heat planning; keep gas network; shut coal only when alternatives exist; storage / power-to-heat (converting surplus electricity into heat) / electrolyzers — no forced fossil-plant replacement timetable or dynamic heat tariffs
science-based BEW decarbonization roadmap replacing plants with large heat pumps; expand district heating for affordable climate-neutral heat; community heat options

fully renewable heat by 2035; heat-transition fund and renovations that stay neutral for warm rents; accelerate district heating and remunicipalize key heat infrastructure; transparent municipal heat planning
push the heat transition in older buildings; climate-neutral buildings via renovation without extra tenant burden; coal phase-out by 2030; new builds to Passive House level
cellSummaries.nuclear-energy::afd: return to nuclear power as part of a technology-open mix; make Berlin a center of nuclear research again; modern 3rd/4th-generation reactors for baseload
cellSummaries.animal-protection::cdu: ban selling pets in public places; stronger control of online platforms; tougher federal penalties for illegal pet trade
cellSummaries.animal-protection::spd: strengthen veterinary services against illegal animal trade; ban animals on state stages and circuses with wild animals; public spaces as habitat for urban nature and animals
cellSummaries.animal-protection::gruene: mandatory origin proof in the dog register against illegal puppy trade; lasting funding for shelters, pet food banks and wildlife stations plus an emergency fund; expand animal-free research and gradually replace animal experiments
cellSummaries.animal-protection::linke: strengthen animal rights: independent state animal-welfare commissioner, law giving organizations standing to sue; plan to phase out animal testing, funding for the Berlin animal shelter and animal food/help bank, neutering street cats; abolish the list of “dangerous” dog breeds
cellSummaries.animal-protection::fdp: protect dogs from stigmatization, to improve their chances of adoption from shelters; measures on pigeons: closing wild nesting sites, deterrence measures, Ovistop pigeon fertility control, if ineffective — pest-control rules
cellSummaries.animal-protection::afd: abolish dog tax; second state-run shelter; state subsidy for Berlin shelter energy costs; more veterinary-office staff; strengthen 3R research to reduce animal experiments (not a research ban)
cellSummaries.animal-protection::bsw: animal protection as a state task; phase out animal testing with funding priority for animal-free methods; stable basic funding for shelters and organizations; multi-year funding, crisis fund, and cost coverage after confiscations
cellSummaries.animal-protection::volt: plan urban development and animal protection together; green-blue corridors linking streets, canals and parks for wildlife; ban breeding and use of wild animals for entertainment
cellSummaries.animal-protection::tierschutz: species-protection program; wildlife-safe city bins; phase out animal testing; fund the shelter and expand freeroaming-cat neutering; phase out selling animals in pet stores; no circus animal keeping/acts on state land
cellSummaries.animal-protection::oedp: stricter protection of city trees and hedges as habitats; keep Tempelhofer Feld and water bodies for animals too; preserve Berlin forests; ban research animal testing and create a chair for animal-free research
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::cd: firm “no” to a rent cap (Mietendeckel); instead a rent-price review office and free energy advice
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::sp: goal: a legally robust rent cap (Mietendeckel) via a federal opening clause for the states or Article 15 of the Basic Law; new rent oversight; rent-price check app
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::gr: Affordable Rents Act: owners with more than 50 apartments must rent a share of new leases at least 20% below the average price; calculate the rent index (Mietspiegel) over 20 years instead of 6; rent cap (Mietendeckel) via a federal opening clause for the states
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::li: rent cap for municipal housing (LWU) within the first 100 days: one-year freeze, then max 1% increase per year in the Housing Supply Act; push a federal rent cap; commercial rent cap to protect small shops, daycares, Spätis and clubs
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::fd: against a rent cap (Mietendeckel); “rents TÜV” review of laws that raise building costs and rents; annual rent index (Mietspiegel) based on real data without political influence
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::af: no price regulation: “the best brake on prices is sufficient housing supply,” so remove obstacles to private renting; instead housing benefit top-ups for WBS holders and full transparency of heating bills and heat contracting
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::bs: another attempt at a rent cap (Mietendeckel): Bundesrat initiative for a nationwide cap in tight markets such as Berlin, or to let the states introduce it themselves; enforce existing rental rules consistently
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::vo: against rigid rent caps (Mietendeckel) and blanket expropriations — evidence that they shrink supply and slow modernization; keep the rent brake (Mietpreisbremse) in tight-market neighborhoods, simplify checks of permissible rent, and introduce a tamper-proof digital housing database for rent-index transparency and to expose vacancies and speculation
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::ti: restore a binding state rent cap (Mietendeckel) for public housing stock: new leases at least 10% below the local comparative rent, WBS apartments at max €6.50/m², warm rent capped at 30% of income with protection against termination during temporary payment hardship; statewide rent register and a landlord license
cellSummaries.housing-rent-regulation-mietendeckel::oe: fair tenancy law against rack-renting and property speculation; housing should not primarily serve investor interests
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::cd: Berlin housing offensive: 100,000 new apartments by 2031; standardized Berlin multi-family house (Berlin-MFH); cut environmental, species and heritage-protection rules back to the minimum required by federal/EU law
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::sp: large public/cooperative new-build push (majority of new homes with LWU, co-ops and nonprofits; 100,000 in 2026–2031); raise social-housing share in the cooperative land model to 50%; curb demolition and tackle neglected/junk properties
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::gr: building turnaround: use resources better, avoid vacancy, prevent demolition where possible; office-to-housing conversion support and a moratorium on new office buildings while over 2.2 million m² of offices stand empty; Schumacher timber district
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::li: up to €2 billion a year in equity for state-owned housing companies to build 7,500 municipal apartments annually, permanently affordable
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::fd: add residential floors on retail and other suitable sites; develop new neighborhoods; partially cancel some well-connected inner-city allotment gardens for housing (keep/create gardens outside the center); start Tempelhofer Feld edge development immediately; resume selling surplus state building plots; allow voluntary conversion of vacant commercial, office and shop space into housing
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::af: more rental housing by cutting barriers for private investment; streamline the Berlin building code; for approved new builds, skip separate demolition permits for prior structures; ease rules so alterations and new builds are easier
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::bs: binding target of at least 6,000 new social-housing units per year, permanently social; stop selling state land — long-term leasehold mainly to municipal housing companies and non-profit cooperatives; Berlin student-housing fund to build affordable dorm places within five years
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::vo: secure land for 300,000 new apartments in the urban development plan to 2040; simplify converting vacant commercial and existing space into housing (room for 30,000 apartments in existing buildings); extra storeys, flexible standards, and digital-map/satellite searches for vacant and infill sites; apply heritage and neighborhood protection more flexibly; use the Hamburg standard for faster, cheaper building
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::ti: reuse before new build: convert vacant offices, oversized shopping centers and underused properties into housing, social facilities, culture and education; densify only on already sealed or underused sites such as single-story commercial buildings, parking lots and supermarket plots; mandatory high ecological and energy standards for new projects
cellSummaries.housing-new-construction-and-targets::oe: against excessive densification that endangers green space and allotment gardens; municipal land only for municipal and cooperative housing; housing before offices; convert vacant industrial buildings into housing; revive social housing under city ownership; goal: 15-minute city of short distances
cellSummaries.housing-socialization-of-large-landlords: categorical “no” to expropriations and compulsory administration

no program to socialize large landlords; cites the “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.” referendum as proof Berliners reject rent-gouging by big listed firms; grow public stock via LWU/co-ops and targeted purchases instead

implement “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.”; keep pushing socialization as legally possible and financeable; for speculative vacancy after six months — compulsory administration and, as a last resort, socialization
implement the “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.” referendum result (59.1%, ~220,000 apartments) through a socialization law

reject expropriation and socialization of private apartments — “this creates not a single new apartment,” wastes billions and scares off investors; reject expropriation/socialization plans as alien to the Basic Law and oppose reinterpretations of Article 15 GG; protect the right to property and already acquired ownership
strictly reject expropriation of housing companies; instead foster an investment-friendly climate for private rental construction
implement the “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.” referendum; for prolonged vacancy without good reason, examine trustee letting through the district; socialization remains a last resort

reject blanket expropriations — evidence they shrink supply, slow modernization and tie up billions in compensation needed for new builds; instead a “price anchor” by massively expanding municipal and cooperative stock toward up to 50% socially oriented housing

socialize large housing portfolios under Article 15 GG; several legal opinions confirm it can be done constitutionally; implement “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.” with public administration and fair compensation — transfer to socially oriented management for stable rents, less displacement and democratic control

no explicit socialization of large landlords; essential public services of general interest “must without exception return to public ownership”; tax to curb land speculation on designated vacant building land
cellSummaries.housing-municipal-stock-social-housing-w: expand municipal housing companies’ stock to 500,000 apartments with equity injections; digitalize WBS (Wohnberechtigungsschein / eligibility certificate) and housing-benefit applications; target social housing at those who need it, with income checks on re-letting

public housing construction program; more than half of new builds via municipal companies, cooperatives and other common-good landlords; raise social-housing share in the cooperative building-land model to 50%; broaden WBS eligibility for single parents

further develop municipal housing companies as lasting common-good actors; raise the WBS (eligibility certificate) quota in allocations; Genossenschaftspakt (“cooperative pact”) for bureaucracy reduction, financing and land access

grow the ~400,000 municipal apartments (LWU), including Berlinovo as a seventh company, and keep buying stock; inside the S-Bahn ring, 100% of vacated LWU units to WBS households (up to WBS 220); landlords with >1,000 units must let every second re-let affordably

municipal housing companies build simple modular apartments on state land and focus on energy renovation of their stock; long term, prefer subject subsidies (housing benefit) over object subsidies for social housing; districts get a share of proceeds from state land sales

priority for long-term Berlin residents when allocating municipal and subsidized housing, via a points system (“apartments are not asylum shelters”); supplement housing benefit with rent top-ups for WBS holders; reintroduce a misallocation levy (Fehlbelegungsabgabe) on social housing
binding target of at least 6,000 new social-housing units per year, mainly via municipal companies; public subsidies only with permanent rent and occupancy ties so units stay social housing

raise the common-good housing stock toward up to 50% (cooperatives, municipal companies, multigenerational and employer housing) via hereditary building right (Erbbaurecht); keep social quotas on large new builds; Fehlbelegungsabgabe (misallocation levy) earmarked for new social housing; social rental agency to sublet market flats to low-income tenants

state rent cap for the public stock; WBS apartments at max €6.50/m²; sharply raise the mandatory social-housing quota in new builds; strengthen a land/housing fund with credit lines and active buy-backs of buildings hit by vacancy, decay or insolvency
revive and expand social housing under municipal management; strengthen municipal housing companies and cooperatives and give them priority when selling public land and property
cellSummaries.housing-vacancy-tourist-apartments-specu: strengthen enforcement against misuse of housing (Zweckentfremdung); introduce property tax C (Grundsteuer C) on build-ready vacant plots; apply building orders (Baugebote) when permits sit unused for two years
tighten the ban on misuse of housing and cut allowed holiday-let days; vacancy reporting duty and a progressive vacancy tax

tighten the Zweckentfremdung ban (min. €50,000 fine) and further curb holiday lets; after six months of vacancy — compulsory administration, socialization as last resort; property tax C and strict building orders against land speculation

comprehensive ban on holiday apartments in residential buildings; abolish the “Berliner Linie” and replace it with a vacancy law; occupying housing vacant for at least a year should lead to lasting housing rights unless owners commit to reletting at socially acceptable rents

act more firmly against speculative vacancy; for prolonged vacancy without good reason, examine trustee letting through the district; effectively ban converting apartments into tourist accommodation and reorganize district staffing for enforcement
tamper-proof digital housing database to make rents transparent and expose vacancy and speculation; digitally map vacant commercial space for reuse
end vacancy, punish misuse of housing, and strictly control holiday apartments — with clearly more staff so checks and reactivation actually happen
cellSummaries.housing-ownership-conversion-of-rental-a: Berlin ownership bonus for first owner-occupied purchase (€10k per adult, €5k per child); keep the conversion ordinance as tenant protection; reject a permanent privatization ban

make the ban on converting rentals to condominiums permanent; limit personal-use evictions to the nuclear family and ban “purchased” personal use; ban index-linked leases and cut the rent-increase cap to max 6% over three years; stop passing property tax to tenants; protect tenants already living in a flat when it is converted
stop converting rentals into condos; make the conversion ban permanent; make owner-occupancy evictions much harder

permanent ban on converting rentals to condominiums; constitutional ban on privatizing municipal housing; “personal use” eviction only for first-degree relatives with stronger hardship protection; statewide database of such evictions and a public transparency register

Only 16 % of Berliners live in their own home → permit the conversion of rental apartments into condominiums throughout the city (tenant protections remain), repeal bans on such conversions, abolish areas with special protection against displacement, and do not exercise the city’s right of first refusal
limit Milieuschutz zones’ side effects (investment/new-build chill); ease rules so alterations and new builds are easier; help tenants become owners — no position on personal-use evictions

protect tenants from displacement, luxury modernization and condo conversions; expand neighborhood-protection zones; require owners to allow same-rent apartment swaps; legally secure the city’s right of first refusal
cellSummaries.housing-tax-on-the-first-property-purcha: cut real-estate transfer tax on a first owner-occupied purchase: waive it on up to €300k of the price when the purchase is ≤ €800k; claw back if sold within 10 years

raise real-estate transfer tax by 0.5 percentage points overall; exceptions for owner-occupiers; possible lower self-use rate after a federal Share-Deal crackdown — not a blanket first-buyer exemption
raise real-estate transfer tax at least to Brandenburg’s level and socially stagger it: owner-occupiers pay less, large companies and Share Deals pay more
no first-buyer real-estate transfer tax relief; raise the rate from 6.0% to 8.0% (at least Brandenburg’s 6.5%)
cut real-estate transfer tax for owner-occupied purchases: first €750,000 of the price tax-free, remainder at the normal rate; financed by selling state building land
fully abolish real-estate transfer tax for domestic first-time buyers of owner-occupied homes; introduce 20% real-estate transfer tax for investors based outside the EU
no first-buyer real-estate transfer tax allowance; Bundesrat initiative for stricter Share-Deal limits so housing corporations cannot dodge the tax while ordinary buyers pay
federal initiative: one-time real-estate transfer tax allowance of €36,000 per person — effectively a full exemption up to €600,000 purchase price per person
progressive real-estate transfer tax: allowances for those with little land ownership, higher rates for larger holdings — ease access for housing projects/co-ops and curb land speculation
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::cdu: fight homelessness with early help and stronger structures; Housing First as one approach; more suitable offers especially for women experiencing homelessness
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::spd: end homelessness by 2030; create a SozialWohnWerk (social housing works) including conversion of vacant offices; 2,500 apartments in the protected market segment under Housing First
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::grue: expand Housing First with municipal companies for unconditional access to one’s own home; push for an eviction moratorium and a prevention concept against homelessness
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::link: no municipal forced evictions for rent arrears; double the protected housing market to 2,500 apartments/year; 10% of new/re-lets of municipal and funded housing for people affected by homelessness
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::fdp: comprehensive Housing First strategy; municipal companies should also provide housing for people at risk of homelessness; consistently prevent homeless camps while offering alternative accommodation
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::afd: combat homelessness: many homeless people lack a German passport and a long-term prospect of staying, so use return options more actively; help should be “targeted, humane and realistic”
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::bsw: over 55,000 homeless, at least 6,000 on the street, risk of up to 100,000 by decade’s end; Housing First puts the apartment first with voluntary support (Finland: ~€15,000 saved per person/year)
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::volt: statewide Housing First building program: a private apartment and support instead of costly collective shelters; Finland’s example — homelessness down ~80%
cellSummaries.housing-evictions-and-homelessness::tier: early intervention on rent arrears (mediation, free debt counseling); anchor Housing First as a basic principle so no one is forced onto the street
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::cdu: Expand the list of “high-crime locations,” security on public transport, “effective, forceful justice (schlagkräftige Justiz)”
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::spd: Community Policing, foot and bicycle patrols, personnel on U- and S-Bahn, investment program for police stations
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::gruene: prevention as the main tool: youth social and cultural work in poor neighborhoods (especially for young men); make police training more attractive
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::linke: measure security not by policing criteria but by addressing social causes; examine whether staff growth is needed (comparison with other city-states), and abandon the increasingly costly expansion of powers; “more police” does not mean more safety for BIPoC and trans people; strengthen only water-police oversight
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::fdp: More police and neighborhood contact officers, “no-go areas are unacceptable,” renovate stations; better equipment and more staff for police, the judiciary, fire services, and emergency services; “prevention before repression, but where necessary — consistent enforcement of the law”
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::afd: mobile police stations in problem neighborhoods and a denser network of fixed stations; more staff for police, judiciary and fire service; area-wide video surveillance of hotspots
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::bsw: More police presence and better equipment, more staff and better training, plus “smart prevention” — but “without blanket surveillance or prejudgment”; community-oriented police and swift justice
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::volt: Clearance rate below 50 percent: prevention (street outreach, youth welfare, men in social professions, exit programs) plus more police and judicial staff for denser patrols and consistent punishment; sensible division of tasks between the police and public-order service so police officers can focus on core duties
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::tiersc: expand police stations especially in outer districts; neighborhood officers and community policing; independent police complaints office and police commissioner
cellSummaries.security-police-in-neighborhoods::oedp: Proper staffing and equipment for police, fire services, and the judiciary, “equal legal certainty for all Kieze,” Kontaktbeamte and bicycle units on the streets
cellSummaries.security-video-surveillance-and-biometri: expand intelligent video surveillance at crime hotspots and on public transport
against indiscriminate mass surveillance and biometric facial recognition, against data retention (Vorratsdatenspeicherung); extend data-protection powers to law-enforcement agencies as well

against linking police databases with video surveillance and checks without suspicion — this is a “gateway” to racial profiling and discriminatory police action; review the necessity of data retention and access rights to government databases, and give the data-protection commissioner more resources

temporary video surveillance and Security by Design (lighting, open sightlines, no dark corners), but the costs and benefits of indiscriminate video surveillance must be assessed and it should be dismantled if necessary; delete the “Szenekunde Sport” database
comprehensive video surveillance of all “hot spots,” plus cameras at illegal-dumping hot spots; at the same time, data protection and privacy are declared “non-negotiable”
video surveillance only where high crime has been demonstrated — with parliamentary authorization and enough staff to analyze recordings in real time; 96-hour retention period for BVG and DB cameras
supports bodycams in Berlin (transparency, de-escalation), with mandatory activation and full equipment for all officers involved

rejects video surveillance in public space and data retention (Vorratsdatenspeicherung), excludes automatic facial recognition, and permits biometrics only in narrow exceptions by court order; Quick-Freeze procedure instead of data retention, strict regulation of drones, and exclusion of Social Scoring and AI-based behavioral analysis
cellSummaries.security-suspicionless-checks-and-contro: allow suspicionless identity checks in public spaces
limit suspicionless checks to a necessary minimum; violence-prevention law (Gewaltpräventionsgesetz); strengthen the independent police and citizens commissioner
reject suspicionless checks and introduce a digital stop-and-search receipt; review high-crime designation zones and weapon-ban zones and abolish them where needed
abolish suspicionless checks: they disproportionately affect young people perceived as having a migrant background; end corresponding police powers
special powers to establish identity and search without suspicion remain, but the criteria for classifying a place as “crime-burdened” should be clarified in the ASOG

more police checks without suspicion in problem neighborhoods and expanded checks without suspicion in high-crime locations; nighttime curfew for underage high-intensity offenders (Intensivtäter), absolute ban on face coverings at assemblies; ✗ knife-ban zones are “purely symbolic politics”
no direct position on checks without suspicion; emphasis on prevention, exit programs, and safe public space through lighting and greenery, plus body cameras as a de-escalation tool
end checks without suspicion: police measures must be justified, proportionate, and reviewable; eliminate discriminatory disparities in police practice and ban pain-compliance techniques
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::cdu: strengthen asset seizure against organized crime and clans; anonymous tip line for drugs/OK; beef up IT forensics and specialized units against digital drug crime (e.g. SkyECC); involve the domestic intelligence (Verfassungsschutz); tougher tax/financial crime enforcement
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::spd: Special structures against mafia organizations, extortion, and forced prostitution; confiscation of criminal proceeds
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::grue: Give priority to structural investigations and the “follow the money” approach, link the LKA and public prosecutors, combat money laundering and tax loopholes
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::link: a single financial-crime authority built on three pillars — police, customs, and tax investigation — under one roof and with shared IT (money laundering, illegal employment, schemes such as Cum-Ex); special units in the LKA and specialized public-prosecution departments, including against digital violence and deepfakes
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::fdp: Combat clan structures and provide prevention so teenagers have alternatives to entering them; merge the Berlin and Brandenburg services for the protection of the constitution
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::afd: Berlin is called the “capital of organized crime” (66 investigation complexes, 485 suspects in 2023), while organized and clan crime are described as “predominantly imported”: the response is a consistent “remigration policy” and deportation of criminal foreigners, a special unit in the immigration authority, and security and crime-fighting in prisons
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::volt: develop BKA “Radar”-style decision support in Berlin; tackle whole criminal networks with European/international partners; stop OK hiding behind concealed assets; push federal reverse burden of proof; expand capacity against financial crime
cellSummaries.security-organized-crime-and-money::tier: Pursue organized crime resolutely, but “without placing entire population groups under blanket suspicion”: origin and family affiliation cannot be grounds for state action; emphasis on dismantling illegal financial and property structures, use a real-estate and assets register against money laundering, plus education, integration, and exit programs
cellSummaries.security-oversight-prevention-support-fo: victim protection via Istanbul Convention state action plan, more women’s shelter places (incl. a 10th women’s shelter), electronic ankle monitors for high-risk offenders; equip social workers
Independent police commissioner, violence-prevention law, femicide risk assessments
state victim-protection act with a right to support; Berlin’s periodic security report on offences and their causes

shift funds from police symbolic politics to social work and crisis services; abolish crime hotspots and weapons-ban zones as gateways for racial profiling; “School against the Right”; no Bundeswehr recruitment in schools; stop police armament and redistribute funds
Delete the the “scene-intelligence sports database” scene-intelligence database database and assess indiscriminate surveillance; prevention before repression, swift courts, and no procedural delays

Mandatory reporting procedure and police involvement in violence against teachers, violence prevention in school lessons, “general prevention”; outpatient support for families through Familienpflege, Familienrat, and family counseling

Against domestic violence — the Spanish model (electronic ankle monitor when a restraining order is imposed and a victim notification system) by court order, expansion of the women’s-shelter network and multilingual guidance on assistance; multiprofessional teams in schools

State strategy for queer safety and a concept against far-right extremism, racism, and antisemitism; regional centers for victims of extremist, racist, and anti-queer violence — psychologists, legal assistance, emergency help; electronic ankle monitors for perpetrators of domestic violence and at least 330 additional places in women’s shelters to fully put in place the Istanbul Convention; digital sexualized violence as a separate form of violence; the Barnahus model for children and British MARAC

Women’s shelters meeting the Istanbul Convention standard (2,5 places per 10 000 residents — not met in Berlin), training for police, the judiciary, and public authorities on Hate Speech, stalking, and femicide, low-threshold online counseling; expand victim–offender mediation (Täter-Opfer-Ausgleich); school social work in every school as prevention
Substantially expand prevention in social services and healthcare; adequate staffing with educators, social workers, and psychologists in schools as early prevention
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::cdu: Kita-Chancenjahr — effectively the return of a preparatory year, family portal with automatic applications
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::spd: Automatic daycare voucher at the first birthday; better child-to-staff ratio and higher share of qualified staff (only staff actually present count); expand language support (heritage-language surcharge, mandatory language-level checks, language daycares); strengthen integration daycares, daycare social work, and municipal providers; mandatory final daycare year citywide
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::gruene: Daycare voucher automatically by the first birthday — with a multilingual letter and QR code for counseling; daycare as a place for learning and free play, not merely supervision; improve the child-to-staff ratio and expand language education
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::linke: fee-free education from Kita to university; focus on Kita quality, staffing and child protection; expand free after-school care (eFöB/Hort) and free meals further up the grades
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::fdp: Issue the voucher automatically together with the birth certificate, language diagnostics in Kita, more independently operated Kitas with the same funding as municipal ones; remove administrative barriers to expanding places and broaden preschool preparation in Kita during the year before school
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::afd: Maintain and expand places according to need, improve the child-to-staff ratio, extend opening hours for parents with special schedules, “blue-light” daycare for police, fire and emergency services, support small and medium providers and workplace daycares; German as the mandatory language in daycare
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::bsw: Mandatory Kita attendance from age four at the latest; regular language diagnostics from age three; neighborhood mothers (Stadtteilmütter) and integration guides to involve parents; restore a binding preschool phase for language, numbers, and social learning
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::volt: Mandatory quality standards: enshrine ratios of 1:3 in nursery groups and 1:7,5 in Kita in law, expand workforce training, organize career changes, and accelerate recognition of foreign diplomas; multiprofessional teams in Kitas and a Berlin Kita-Rat comprising science, practice, and providers (Träger); language support where families already are — in Kita, not through a separate appointment; mandatory and supported transition to school
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::tierschutz: Right to a full-day place for every child from age one regardless of parents’ employment; make Kita-Navigator an up-to-date and reliable placement tool; expand language support — the 40% non-German-origin benchmark does not reflect actual need; relieve educators of admin work and fund admin staff even for small Kitas; strengthen multilingual offerings in bilingual Kitas
cellSummaries.kitas-access-and-quality::oedp: “Quality over quantity” and evaluation of educational quality in daycares; parenting wage for parents as genuine freedom of choice; targeted support for bilingual children by trained staff
cellSummaries.schools-language-and-preparation-for-fir: “No one starts school without fluent German,” emphasis on German and mathematics in primary school
Support family languages: record languages and offer first-language lessons, expand the Europa-Schule network, separate support for refugee children
expand State Europe Schools especially in the east; examine creating German-Arabic or German-Kurdish school branches; expand heritage-language teaching; add Arabic and Kurdish as foreign languages
Language diagnostics already in Kita, funding for language support according to actual need

Enshrine German as the language of school in the school law, ban gender-inclusive language, bring back handwritten cursive; mandatory language-proficiency checks starting in Kita and expansion of “German guarantee classes” in primary schools with a high share of children whose home language is not German
no separate measures on school language: emphasis on “reading, writing and arithmetic” as the core of primary school; mandatory integration measures and language learning for adult migrants

Mandatory preschool phase from age five — about one-third of children have language deficits; language tests at age four with support from qualified language teachers; joint support planning by Kita and primary school with regular exchange; France’s mandatory Vorschule from age three as a reference
at school entry: evidence-based language assessment plus binding low-threshold support; interpreters for parent talks
“Integration means removing language barriers”: early educational opportunities for bilingual children and support for both languages by trained staff in parent-child groups and Kitas
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::cdu: More German and mathematics, school sports with an “achievement ethos”
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::spd: All types of school-leaving qualification at every school, mandatory 11th year, full inclusion
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::grue: Individual support without pressure; double the number of comprehensive schools; a perspectives year for young people without a school-leaving qualification or apprenticeship place (more than 8% leave without a qualification); democratize schools by funding student councils; keep family centers at primary schools
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::link: More comprehensive schools, abolish student selection (“casting”), oppose school segregation
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::fdp: More school self-governance and staffing autonomy; dual teacher-education degrees; use vacant and underused premises (e.g. at upper secondary centers) before converting schools to another type; cut school bureaucracy
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::afd: Restore “discipline and the will to achieve”: behavior grades, discipline agreements, “time-out rooms” for disruptive students, German flag at every school; entrance tests for Gymnasium and the option to transfer students back out of Gymnasium
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::bsw: End the teacher shortage, high-quality comprehensive schools, curriculum reform; “the best opportunities regardless of parents’ wallets”
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::volt: A school that “supports and challenges”: easier movement between school types, transparent criteria and better counseling for students and parents, more schools with their own upper-secondary level or reliable cooperation, develop existing school types instead of dismantling the system; support gifted students — MINT programs, competitions, and school academies; multiprofessional teams in schools
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::tier: Reform the school system: less early sorting, more Gemeinschaftsschule years, allot some places by lottery for social mixing, and ease school-type changes in the transition; renovate dilapidated buildings — new build only where modernization is not enough (acoustics, light, air); schools as places of lived democracy, with an Antragsrecht for students in school-wide bodies
cellSummaries.schools-structure-and-requirements::oedp: “Heart and mind” as the school’s central task; free learning materials without copy fees; lessons for all the senses — music, media literacy, cooking, crafts, theater, school garden
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::cdu: equip every school with sufficient qualified social pedagogues — not literally one person per school
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::spd: A social worker in every school, recording teachers’ working time, ban on mobile phones in all primary schools
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::gruen: More school social workers and multiprofessional teams without cutting teacher numbers; paid Teamzeiten for collaboration; keep Familienzentren at primary schools
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::linke: Restore 470 cut positions; special education fund (off-budget investment package)
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::fdp: Abolish civil-servant status for teachers (Verbeamtung); relieve teachers and school leadership of administrative work; provide an IT specialist for each school or school cluster
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::afd: In the teacher-training law, shift emphasis from “Diversity,” “Queer,” and “Gender” topics to didactics and practical work; give priority to moving fee-based teachers into permanent positions without unjustified fixed-term contracts
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::bsw: Remove smartphones and tablets from primary-school classrooms; multiprofessional teams of teachers, educators, social workers, psychologists, and specialists in IT, prevention, and administration
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::volt: Multiprofessional teams and recruitment of men into social and psychological professions as role models; tackle staff shortages by expanding training, organizing career changes, and rapidly recognizing foreign diplomas
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::tiers: School social work in every school with permanent rather than annually reviewed funding; deep expansion of SIBUZ and school psychology; tackle teacher shortages via continued civil-servant status (Verbeamtung), less bureaucracy, multiprofessional teams, dual teacher training, and mentoring for career changers; fair pay and fewer fixed-term contracts in social professions
cellSummaries.schools-staff-social-work-screens::oedp: Against early and excessive digital learning in primary school — children need motor and sensory experience and teamwork with real people; adequate staffing with educators, social workers, and psychologists; recruit teachers by cutting bureaucracy in recognizing foreign diplomas and offering a relocation allowance
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::cdu: Recognize foreign diplomas faster and recruit more workers into skilled trades, care, education, police, fire services, and municipal companies; promote master crafts training with a master-crafts training bonus, because without good craftspeople the city does not run
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::spd: recruit international skilled workers (especially care); speed recognition of foreign degrees; skilled-workers strategy and stronger school-to-work links
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::gru: recruit international skilled workers with Welcome Center support, faster transparent recognition of foreign degrees, and fair coordinated recruitment abroad
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::lin: Staff shortages across sectors, worsened by lack of affordable housing; train and retain more skilled workers in Berlin instead of only poaching from elsewhere; faster recognition of foreign qualifications
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::fdp: Fight staff shortages in education (daycares and schools): better child-to-staff ratio, relieve teachers and leadership of bureaucracy, dual teacher-education degrees, IT specialists for schools; immigration of people ready to work when skills are scarce
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::afd: fight skills shortage mainly via dual training, further training and retraining for people already here; reject the apprenticeship levy; medical places in Berlin instead of recruiting abroad; restrictive migration overall
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::bsw: End the teacher shortage; multiprofessional teams in schools; easier recognition of foreign school and vocational qualifications; Ausbildungsoffensive at home; skilled immigration only where it does not create shortages in origin countries
