cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::vol: Staff shortages are holding back the economy; modernize the immigration authority (LEA) with fully digital applications and stronger specialist units; speed recognition of foreign diplomas via digital interfaces; build a real Welcome Center; Denmark’s SIRI as a model for a central digital contact point
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::tie: address shortages of teachers, educators, and social-care professionals through workforce policy, collective-agreement linkage, fewer fixed-term contracts, and more training places; no separate measure on recruitment from abroad in the fragments found
cellSummaries.shortage-of-qualified-professionals::oed: Recruit more teachers by cutting bureaucracy in recognizing foreign diplomas and offering a relocation allowance; constant teacher shortage noted alongside the need for adequate school staffing
cellSummaries.vocational-education-and-dual-training::: Treat vocational and academic education as equal; make Meister, Techniker and Fachwirt training free of charge; a “Tag des Handwerks” at secondary schools; faster recognition of foreign vocational qualifications

Strengthen dual training with an apprentice hub for housing and support, keep the apprentice ticket, implement the apprenticeship levy; develop the youth careers agency and youth career support; improve the 11th compulsory school year and the integrated vocational training year for the school-to-work transition

Flexible perspectives year instead of a rigid 11th compulsory school year; stronger career guidance and at least five workplace insights in grades 8–10; dual training as equal to university via a levy-funded training guarantee and an apprentice hub

Strengthen training partnerships especially in craft trades; apprenticeship levy to relieve training firms; support young people leaving school without an apprenticeship place; better school-to-training transition and an apprentice hub
Schools should prepare for vocational training or university; dual teacher education, more school autonomy and focus on German, maths and practical skills

Strengthen in-company dual training and reject the apprenticeship levy; raise master-craftsman BAföG, master start-up bonus, Dutch-style further-training fund; stronger school–chamber cooperation and career guidance

Expand career-oriented school internships (Schülerpraktika) to three two-week block placements so young people see craft trades and choose apprenticeships more consciously; credit practicum performance on school reports
Strengthen dual training as equal to university; central overview of open apprenticeship places; Berliner Azubiwerk for affordable housing; Ausbildungsplatzgarantie modeled on Vienna’s guarantee

Treat apprenticeship and university as equal paths; Ausbildungsgarantie and minimum trainee pay; at least three one-week Praktika in lower secondary plus structured support into training, study, or voluntary service
School lessons for all the senses with more weight on practical life subjects — crafts (Werken), cooking, theater, school garden — as hands-on preparation alongside academic learning
cellSummaries.higher-education::cdu: Berlin as a center for science and innovation: medicine, biotechnology, artificial intelligence, startups; universities and research centers as part of the economic strategy
cellSummaries.higher-education::spd: “medical capital,” a strong Charité, science and future industries — artificial intelligence, DeepTech, aerospace, railway technology, games, finance, and defense
cellSummaries.higher-education::gruene: Restore reliable higher-education contracts with higher funding and planning security; strengthen the student services organization; keep Berlin attractive for students and researchers through fair conditions and university autonomy
cellSummaries.higher-education::linke: Keep university study tuition-free including for international students; raise student-services funding; expand civil clauses (no military research); strengthen university teacher education with extra funding toward 3,000 teaching graduates a year
cellSummaries.higher-education::fdp: Universities as “beacons of excellence” competing for the best minds; Tenure-Tracks as standard; lock in freedoms via a Berliner university freedom law (Hochschulfreiheitsgesetz) and continued university contracts (Hochschulverträge)
cellSummaries.higher-education::afd: Defend academic freedom against cancel culture and ideology on campus; strengthen university autonomy; expand medical and pharmacy study places in Berlin rather than recruiting doctors from abroad
cellSummaries.higher-education::bsw: raise state subsidies (Landeszuschüsse) toward ≥2% of GDP; Studentenwohnheim fund; Zivilklausel; end chain contracts; prioritize MINT
cellSummaries.higher-education::volt: Reliable long-term basic funding for Berlin’s universities; more study places in MINT, teaching, and health; better study conditions (counseling, family-friendly research); transparent career paths including Tenure-Track
cellSummaries.higher-education::tierschutz: more training places in social professions, fewer fixed-term contracts, and equal pay; higher education should be accessible, socially equitable, and non-discriminatory
cellSummaries.higher-education::oedp: Better maintenance of education buildings for a pleasant learning atmosphere; promote student housing
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::cdu: Lifelong learning as a fourth pillar: strengthen adult education and free providers; a state program for basic skills (Grundbildung); more permanent contracts for adult education center teachers in basic skills and language; expand and coordinate non-formal education
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::spd: Qualification offensive for digitalization, demographics, and climate transition; expand further-training and apprenticeship partnerships; accessible lifelong learning via adult-education centers and the second-chance pathway; make academic continuing education a public university task
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::gru: workforce strategy, support transitions into occupations with labor shortages, family compatibility through workplace nurseries; the economy should be green, social, and innovative
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::lin: continuing education as part of social and ecological transformation, collectively bargained jobs, and a strong public sector
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::fdp: Expand continuing education at universities and in workplaces; a continuing-education law (Weiterbildungsgesetz) for a unified Berlin framework; more pathways out of low-wage work especially for women; age-appropriate lifelong-learning offers for older people
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::afd: prioritize qualifying people already in Berlin via continuing education (Weiterbildung); promote vocational degrees, targeted retraining and lifelong learning instead of migration-first skills policy
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::bsw: continuing education is mentioned mainly through labor and social policy
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::vol: Berliner education pass (BildungsPass): annual continuing-education credit for everyone 25+ at accredited providers; make skills from work, volunteering, and self-study visible via digital credentials; expand part-time and digital formats; modular Teilqualifikationen toward recognized qualifications
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::tie: Jobcenters should advise and train instead of imposing sanctions; more training places in social professions, permanent funding for social work, and fewer fixed-term contracts
cellSummaries.continuing-education-and-retraining::oed: recognize foreign qualifications faster, relocation allowance for skilled workers, cut bureaucracy; teach practical skills and support professionals for education, care, and the social sector
cellSummaries.healthcare-hospitals-and-neighborhood-ca: Charité as a center for innovation, neighborhood health hubs, e-health, gene and cell therapy, less bureaucracy for hospitals
“Medical capital,” a strong Charité, integrated health centers in the districts

Top-level university medicine and neighborhood care are not mutually exclusive; equalize opportunities between districts (outlying and eastern areas without doctors), telemedicine and AI, a public health service, and district health conferences
expand municipal Charité and Vivantes; remunicipalize hospitals where private operators exit; speed municipal and non-profit outpatient centers / neighborhood basic care via a Vivantes taskforce

“Outpatient before inpatient”; modernize emergency services and ease ER load via phone triage; best hospital care 24/7/365; reorder hospital financing around actual patient need and end the old outpatient/inpatient split; cybersecurity in health facilities; Berlin as a model region for telemedicine and health start-ups

Hospitals threatened by insolvency and closures due to inadequate public funding and insurer payments — hurting buildings, technology and staff; raise investment cost subsidies to actual need; more study places for doctors and pharmacists instead of recruiting abroad (Charité cuts called a mistake)

hospitals are part of public infrastructure and “not businesses”: planning in the public interest with resident participation, care close to home and accessible by public transport, targeted support for clinics providing social support and linking outpatient with inpatient care, eliminate an investment backlog of several hundred million €

Expand the state program for integrated health centers (LIG), especially in outlying and structurally weak districts: “houses of care” with multiprofessional teams, midwives, and psychological support, with a health kiosk for older people at each center providing care counseling and therapy; long opening hours relieve emergency departments; multilingual health guides; street triage instead of police during mental-health crises; Senior-Berlin app, recognition of ME/CFS and Long-COVID

Strengthen Rettungsdienst and primary care along the whole chain; nutrition team and plant-based hospital meals (also against antibiotic-resistant infections); free, low-bureaucracy medical care for homeless people via mobile teams
No pursuit of profit in healthcare and care, with money going toward better staff pay; support the establishment of pediatric practices in underserved districts
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::cdu: Statewide Mental Health program and more school psychology for pupils, teachers and families; prevention on movement, nutrition and mental health embedded in everyday school life; citywide drop-in points for young people in crisis; align psychotherapy capacity with real need to cut waiting times
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::spd: Develop a Masterplan for mental health to reorganize support, shorten waiting times and create integrated offers; push KV and federal reforms of needs planning; more therapy places and trained staff; expand contact and counseling centers
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::gruene: Destigmatization, prevention, and early detection, multiprofessional crisis and outreach services in every district, plus dedicated psychological support for refugees
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::linke: Create Berlin’s share of missing psychotherapy statutory health-insurance therapy slots (Kassensitze); oversight of cost reimbursement (Kostenerstattung); outreach therapy for older and immobile people; more clinic places and pay for therapists in training; expand supported housing and psychiatric case work
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::bsw: Loneliness as a political task: neighborhood centers, community projects, and measures against isolation (affecting older and younger people and homeless people); separate shelters for people with addictions because homelessness intensifies mental strain
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::volt: Mental Health in the curriculum, meeting places against loneliness — multigenerational cafés and neighborhood centers, free materials on postnatal depression, intensive support for single parents; mobile Street Triage teams made up of police and the Berliner Krisendienst instead of police alone during mental-health crises
cellSummaries.healthcare-mental-health::tierschutz: Low-threshold psychosocial care regardless of income, origin or residence status; more school psychologists, social workers and therapists in schools and Kitas; mandatory free prevention on stress, bullying, anxiety and depression; raise psychotherapy statutory health-insurance therapy slots (Kassensitze); loneliness strategy with an Einsamkeitsbeauftragte*r
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::cdu: “Outpatient before inpatient” — stay in familiar surroundings as long as possible; expand care support centers; free training for volunteer caregivers; telemedicine and video consultations; neighborhood health hubs for older and mobility-impaired people; a clear central overview of doctors, midwives and care places
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::spd: Support for home care, a cap on out-of-pocket co-payments, collectively bargained pay in care
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::gruene: Chapters “Good care” and “Self-determined seniors”: live self-determined and in dignity at every age; a city enabling participation, solidarity and care; gradually make Berlin an age-friendly city
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::linke: Berlinovo builds its own Pflegewohnen segment; Bundesrat drive to ban Eigenbedarf terminations and forced evictions of seniors; Stadtteilsorgezentren with offers for seniors and family caregivers including low-cost neighborhood canteens/cafés, adequate staffing and short distances
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::fdp: Strengthen ambulatory care so people can stay in their familiar environment; digital marketplace for care and support offers; strengthen district seniors’ representation legally and financially while abolishing the State Seniors’ Advisory Council; self-employed statutory health and care-insurance contributions based only on earned self-employment income
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::afd: Older Berliners face digital exclusion, bureaucracy and a lack of accessible affordable housing; pensions often too low after broken careers and family care/child-raising; demand age-appropriate housing, keep analog access to authorities, and fight loneliness through participation and volunteering
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::bsw: Pensions tax-free up to 2 000 €; care and hospitals in public or nonprofit ownership, review the treatment of care homes during the pandemic, “think together” about Kitas, primary schools, and homes for older people
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::volt: Support family caregivers with digital platforms (chatbot for applications, community) and faster digital applications via the state competence center 4.0; digital guides helping older people; a health kiosk for seniors at every health center; Senior-Berlin app; ageing in place — remain in familiar surroundings
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::tierschutz: Education and social participation for older people, digital support, fall prevention and anti-loneliness projects; pets allowed in seniors’ and care facilities; humane, common-good care with binding staffing ratios; loneliness strategy with an Einsamkeitsbeauftragte*r
cellSummaries.care-pflege-and-older-people::oedp: No profit motive in elder care and funding for better pay; more age-appropriate and affordable housing
cellSummaries.drug-policy::cdu: Fight drug crime hard: smash clan and drug networks; anonymous electronic tip-off system for drug trafficking and organized crime; more prison cell searches with drug- and data-carrier dogs; expand specialized units such as observation teams against organized and digitally networked drug crime
cellSummaries.drug-policy::spd: “Help instead of punishment”: expand Drug-Checking and therapy; abolish “accompanied drinking” under 16; do not push people with addictions from place to place — help where they are while clearing drugs from parks and playgrounds; expand drug consumption rooms (easier setup, longer hours, municipal buildings)
cellSummaries.drug-policy::gruene: “Help instead of punishment”: more supervised drug-consumption rooms and street outreach, shorter waits for therapy, without an abstinence requirement; stricter rules for gambling advertising and expansion of the “Oasis” self-exclusion database
cellSummaries.drug-policy::linke: Fundamentally different drug policy: do not criminalize use or stigmatize users; continue expanding supervised consumption rooms and inhalation rooms for crack on the Swiss model; end strict pursuit of micro-dealing; expand drug-checking (also mobile and in consumption rooms); more outpatient therapy and psychosocial support
cellSummaries.drug-policy::fdp: Evidence-based “help instead of punishment”: expand drug-checking significantly (also mobile) with a citywide early-warning system; naloxone via recognized addiction help and social work; expand supervised consumption rooms and street-outreach teams; night cafés and consumption rooms in the Kurfürstenkiez; Housing First for homeless users
cellSummaries.drug-policy::bsw: expand prevention and assistance — protected drug consumption rooms, medical support centers, and support for substitution therapy
cellSummaries.drug-policy::volt: assistance instead of criminalization: free mobile drug-checking at clubs (Fixpunkt and Vista laboratories), more supervised consumption rooms with reliable opening hours, expand diamorphine substitution and access to long-term psychotherapy; discontinue cases for possession of small quantities for personal use, raise thresholds through an evidence-based procedure involving addiction medicine and law enforcement; straightforward implementation of the cannabis law and digital applications for grow associations
cellSummaries.drug-policy::tierschutz: prevention instead of repression: addiction is primarily a health and social issue, so provide addiction support, counseling, therapy, and exit programs throughout the city and decriminalize people who use drugs; act firmly against organized, profit-oriented drug trafficking, but without stigmatizing socially vulnerable people
cellSummaries.drug-policy::oedp: Prevention focus: Berlin as a model for non-smoker protection and addiction prevention; ban alcohol advertising in public space and media; remove tobacco and alcohol from checkout areas; extend stricter smoking-venue rules to shisha bars
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::cd: dedicated chapter to organize, manage and limit migration; affirm the right to asylum while keeping state control over migration
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::sp: Defend the right to asylum and implement GEAS in line with human rights; push the federal level to allow state admission programs; integration pathways also for people without protection status or with expiring permits; prioritize returns for serious offenders and security threats without stay rights; early return assistance focused on voluntary return
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::gr: Berlin as a “safe harbor”: resume the state admission program for Syria, Iraq and Afghanistan; fund civilian sea rescue; apply GEAS in line with human rights; deportations only in exceptional cases — not to crisis regions such as Afghanistan, Syria or Iran
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::li: “Every deportation is one deportation too many”; cut-off-date regularization and expanded opportunity-to-stay rights; reject detention, movement restrictions and family separation; state admission programs (e.g. Syria, Afghanistan, Gaza); use temporary deportation stops
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::fd: Increase deportations of people with an enforceable obligation to leave; review Duldung grounds more often; reject a de facto winter deportation freeze; asset checks for asylum seekers (e.g. jewelry, deposits, cash above an allowance) to cover procedure and living costs
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::af: Immediate stop to accepting asylum seekers in Berlin and end voluntary admission of people brought in illegally; convert LEA into an “authority for immigration, asylum and remigration” with priority on returns; Dublin departure center; full cost transparency for asylum policy
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::bs: “Control and limitation without discrimination and racism”; support running all asylum procedures in safe third countries outside the EU — those without a claim to asylum should not enter the EU, which would also remove deportation problems; border controls and refusals at the border until an EU-wide returns deal exists
cellSummaries.migration-admission-and-deportations::ti: deportations are not a topic in the program: assistance should not be blocked by bureaucracy, language, or residence status; refugees without secure status should receive WBS, standards in ASOG shelters reviewed by an independent body
cellSummaries.migration-bezahlkarte-and-access-to-bene: Keep the payment card for asylum benefits and make it permanent; centrally record residence data of people obliged to leave and share it quickly with the competent authorities
reject the payment card for asylum benefits; pursue a Berlin City-ID for access to health, housing, work and education

Abolish the discriminatory payment card; health and social-security rights also without the “right papers”; access to education, healthcare and work regardless of residence status; basic bank account for all

Against the payment card; full standard benefit rate for single refugees in collective housing; social assistance for non-employed EU citizens; equal subsistence benefits and access to work, education and healthcare regardless of status
Berlin, “as the last of the states,” immediately introduces the payment card — both for new arrivals and for those already here
Switch asylum benefits to benefits in kind only; limit supply, counseling and housing to the necessary minimum; cut Berlin top-up benefits; full cost transparency of asylum policy
people entering via a safe third country should have no right to an asylum procedure or social benefits
uniform minimum standards for all Berlin shelters; access to advice and flexible programs regardless of residence status
Reject switching asylum seekers to benefits in kind only
cellSummaries.migration-lea-integration-participation:: State integration centers in every district (language, advice, support in one place); “support and demand” with active participation in language and integration offers required; community work under §5 AsylbLG; faster recognition of foreign qualifications and action against unscrupulous intermediaries; closer cooperation of LEA, refugee authorities, social offices and police to enforce obligations to leave

Professionalize and permanently fund Integrationslots*innen (expanded language groups); central integration and participation monitoring with semi-annual indicators; Berliner city card (CityID) so undocumented people can access health, housing, work and education

Develop LEA into a modern “welcome authority” for ~700,000 Berliners without German or EU citizenship — digital applications, faster processing, stronger ombuds office; strengthen “housing instead of mass shelters” with municipal landlords and shift from mass shelters to decentralized housing

Strengthen LAF staffing and organization; local voting rights for non-citizens after five years; develop the participation law (Partizipationsgesetz) with a binding hiring quota for people with a migration history in the public service
Language and integration courses from day one, mandatory teaching of the foundations of the free democratic basic order, respect for equality, different ways of life, and religious diversity
no language or integration courses for asylum seekers without a right to stay; transform LEA into an “authority for entry, asylum, and remigration”

Broaden integration courses in content — all aspects of living together, rights and obligations “clearly and mandatorily”; require lawful asylum seekers to participate in integration measures and learn the language

Integrated cross-department structure with dedicated posts in LEA and LAF; Welcome Center and integration guides (one-stop); digital LEA–chamber–employer interfaces; “Work Integration Pass” as a European-standard digital skills proof; apprenticeship guarantee on the Vienna model

Language courses regardless of residence status; binding public-service quota for people with a migration history and experience of racism; commissioners for people with a migration history with rights like women’s representatives; Berlin recognition center for foreign qualifications with multilingual advice; no exclusion from the housing market because of flight experience or residence title
Recognize foreign qualifications faster by cutting bureaucracy, relocation allowance for skilled workers, early language support for bilingual children
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::cdu: Mid-sized businesses as the backbone with transformation support; keep Berlin an industrial and startup/digital hub; EXPO 2035 bid with Brandenburg as a future region for innovation
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::spd: Three pillars of industrial policy — mobility, energy technology, pharmaceuticals and medical technology, plus future industries: aerospace, AI and DeepTech, railway technology, games, finance, defense; “medical capital” and science, support for startups (especially those founded by women), Reallaborstrategie, visibility for migrant entrepreneurship
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::gruene: A green, social, and innovative economy: games capital, workforce strategy, Betriebskitas, equal-pay reporting
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::linke: Future-proof Berlin industry and raise industry’s share of value added with collectively bargained jobs; in procurement prioritize Economy for the Common Good firms and companies working with Open Source / digital sovereignty
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::fdp: “Less government, more freedom”; core spending on education, infrastructure, and security; bureaucracy-reduction law, “Frei-Kiez” special economic zone, innovation policy and mandatory Berlin–Brandenburg structures, review of the “uncontrolled proliferation” of municipal companies
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::afd: a central Station-F-style hub for Berlin’s startup ecosystem and research transfer into entrepreneurship; ease unnecessary burdens on SMEs from the switch to fully digital invoicing by 2028
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::bsw: Minimum wage of 15 € per hour through a Bundesrat initiative; preserve Berlin as an industrial location and protect jobs, criticism of high energy prices and bureaucracy; framework conditions and access to venture capital for startups, but criticism of converting Berlin companies and the games industry to defense; abolish fixed-term contracts without objective grounds in the public sector and ensure full application of collective agreements
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::volt: startup capital: central startup hub (Gründungshub) for the Berlin-Brandenburg metro region; KiezLabs (neighborhood labs) in vacant buildings as local innovation hubs; test fields for hydrogen/bidirectional charging (Tegel) and Agri-PV on Tempelhofer Feld
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::tierschutz: eco-social economy for the common good: raise the Land minimum wage to at least €16 with annual inflation indexation; promote mobile work and a four-day week; turn Jobcenters into advice/training places instead of sanctioning; build innovation clusters for circular economy, plant-based food and sustainable mobility; advance open source, AI and quantum tech when they serve the common good
cellSummaries.economy-and-innovation::oedp: Prepare for a post-growth / Economy for the Common Good: Berlin as a city of the Economy for the Common Good with progressive prosperity indicators; tax benefits (e.g. trade-tax multiplier cut by half) for firms with a Common Good Balance Sheet; support regional small businesses and women founders
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::cdu: Berlin as startup capital and digital hub (“Boston on the Spree” for health/biotech); intensify mid-sized businesses–startup–science links; EXPO 2035; bureaucracy “One in – two out”; KI assistant BärGPT for routine city work
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::spd: strengthen future industries (life sciences/health, AI and DeepTech, games, finance, aerospace, rail tech, etc.); continue the Reallabor strategy with funding and a “Made in Berlin” focus; expand support for women founders and access to risk capital
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::gruene: strong innovation ecosystem linking science, business and industrial value creation; a Berlin innovation freedom law (Innovationsfreiheitsgesetz) for real labs, experiment clauses and faster procedures; innovation through international diversity
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::linke: restore the coaching bonus for founders and improve access to credit—for Deep-Tech startups as well as local shops; innovation via public benefit, Open Source and digital sovereignty in procurement (see economy)
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::fdp: strong focus on innovation and business freedom: less bureaucracy, “Frei-Kiez” special economic zone, private investment, startups, artificial intelligence, and joint economic planning with Brandenburg
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::afd: central Station-F-style location for Berlin’s startup ecosystem to strengthen innovation culture and transfer research into entrepreneurship
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::bsw: support startups through access to venture capital and framework conditions, but criticize reorienting the economy and games industry toward defense; main focus on collectively bargained jobs, industry, and less bureaucracy
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::volt: central startup hub (Gründungshub) for Berlin-Brandenburg founders; KiezLabs (neighborhood labs) where local crafts, founders and freelancers grow together; chamber-defined minimum standards for AI/digitalization tools for SMEs
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::tierschutz: eco-social innovation for the common good: clusters for circular economy, plant-based food and sustainable mobility; promote open source; publicly fund AI and quantum technologies when they serve sustainability and the common good
cellSummaries.innovation-and-startups::oedp: Innovation via the Economy for the Common Good and regional small business: tax benefits for firms with a GWÖ Common Good Balance Sheet; programs for women founders; enforce rules against bogus self-employment
cellSummaries.business-succession::cdu: secure business succession with the business-succession center and new networking for generational change in Berlin companies
cellSummaries.business-succession::spd: secure and strengthen the Berlin business-succession center for business succession; bridge to founders and simplify access to innovation and investment funding
cellSummaries.business-succession::gruene: strengthen business succession in craft trades: fee-free and flexible master crafts training, support succession and new starts together with the chambers
cellSummaries.business-succession::linke: secure business succession especially in craft trades with the Chamber of Crafts; protect against rising commercial rents; strengthen training partnerships
cellSummaries.business-succession::afd: promote and simplify business takeovers / succession; master start-up bonus and stronger dual vocational training for crafts
cellSummaries.business-succession::volt: strengthen Berlin’s business-succession center as a one-stop shop for sellers and successors
cellSummaries.small-business::cdu: Support for the mid-sized businesses and crafts: tailored funding for the transition, succession via the business-succession center, fully digital business registration aiming at founding within 24 hours, and less bureaucracy for SMEs
cellSummaries.small-business::spd: Digital “guides” in district economic-development offices, more visibility for migrant entrepreneurship, three further municipal commercial courtyards, a secured business-succession center, and stronger neighborhood retail diversity
cellSummaries.small-business::gruene: Small business as part of an ecological and social economy: a workforce strategy, compatibility of family and work through company childcare centers, equal pay, and climate transformation without job losses
cellSummaries.small-business::linke: Fewer formalities for companies through positive lists and certificates; municipal procurement should support open source, digital sovereignty, fair working conditions, and the public good
cellSummaries.small-business::fdp: Strong emphasis on freedom for business: a law to reduce bureaucracy, less government, private investment, a special economic zone called “Free District,” and a review of which municipal tasks could be performed more efficiently by private providers
cellSummaries.small-business::afd: Exempt small businesses from mandatory E-invoicing; strengthen crafts as the backbone of the mid-sized businesses with a master start-up bonus and easier business takeovers
cellSummaries.small-business::bsw: Preserve the industrial site and jobs, reduce bureaucracy and energy prices; access to capital for startups, but with criticism of reorienting business toward defense
cellSummaries.small-business::volt: Strengthen the business-succession center as a one-stop shop for succession; turn vacant buildings into KiezLabs (neighborhood labs) for crafts, founders and freelancers; IBB loans with repayment grants of up to 40% for certified AI and digitalization solutions
cellSummaries.small-business::tierschutz: No dedicated small-business program; eco-social economy focused on the common good and fair work — higher state minimum wage, mobile work, four-day week; public innovation funding only when it serves the common good and sustainability
cellSummaries.small-business::oedp: Promote regional and small businesses and women founders; tax advantages (e.g. 50% lower trade-tax multiplier) for firms with a Common Good Balance Sheet; stronger enforcement against bogus self-employment
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::cdu: Partial real-estate transfer tax waiver on first owner-occupied purchase (up to €300k share / purchases ≤ €800k); introduce Grundsteuer C on build-ready vacant plots; crack down on transfer-tax avoidance — not a blanket rise in transfer tax
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::spd: invest via budget, SIWA and the federal special fund; raise real-estate transfer tax by 0.5 pp (more for large firms; exceptions for owner-occupiers); packaging tax; priorities housing, transport, energy/heat, schools
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::gruene: Raise and socially stagger real-estate transfer tax; disposable-packaging tax; fight tax evasion as organized crime; federal push for wealth and inheritance-tax reform
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::linke: Luxury-villa tax and stricter audits of the wealthy; raise real-estate transfer tax to 8% (at least Brandenburg’s 6.5%) with room to differentiate; reform and abolish the debt brake; build a Kompetenzzentrum against financial crime including tax investigation
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::fdp: Comply with the “debt brake” without shadow budgets, limit the government share, and give priority to private investment; core spending: education, infrastructure, security; extend the rules to all off-budget funds
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::afd: Restore the “debt brake”: halt debt growth, return to a rules-based budget, and enshrine the debt brake in Berlin’s constitution; borrowing only in exceptional situations
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::bsw: Pensions up to €2,000 tax-free and lower taxes and levies on normal earnings through Bundesrat initiatives; against increasing arms spending at the expense of the social budget, education, healthcare, and culture
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::volt: Tie the budget firmly to the medium-term financial plan, justify deviations publicly, require counter-financing that names the offsets for spending increases, and publish updated budget figures so tax spending is traceable
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::tierschutz: Restore Vermögensteuer; make Grundsteuer and real-estate transfer tax progressive and end passing Grundsteuer on to tenants; keep and, if needed, raise the tourist tax; independent commission against cost overruns on major projects
cellSummaries.taxes-and-budget::oedp: Focus on the common good rather than growth: assess all new city investments by their potential to reduce CO2; tax advantages for companies with a Common Good Balance Sheet
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::cd: Cut bureaucracy; a family portal with automatic applications; combine the management of state holdings and enterprises, professional supervisory boards, and a review of the institution of commissioners and the many councils
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::sp: implement administrative reform with clear responsibilities, central steering and strong districts; digitalization of processes, digital agency and district digitalization guides
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::gr: Administrative reform to end “agency ping-pong”: clear division of responsibilities between the Berlin Senate (Senat) and districts, and the principle of connectivity in the city constitution
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::li: make administration more digital and efficient and bring the administrative reform to life; restore Berlinpass (low-income pass) applications via Bürgerämter (plus a digital proof option for Berlin-Ticket S)
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::fd: comprehensive bureaucracy-relief law and systematic modernization of legislation with digital tools; AI appointment system for citizens’ offices (Bürgerämter) with real-time slot optimization; review which state-owned companies (Landesunternehmen) could deliver services more efficiently under other ownership
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::af: abolish the bloated commissioner system (e.g. equality/anti-discrimination) as costly bureaucracy and clientelism; direct election of the Governing Mayor
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::bs: administration that works and reverse mistaken decisions of prior governments; use AI in places to streamline procedures; stronger staff-council co-determination and health programs in offices; full force of public-service collective agreements and end unfounded fixed-term contracts in the public sector
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::vo: “Berlin works”: first decide who is responsible for what and measure administration by results—clear goals, indicators, binding service standards, and the “three yeses” principle (confirmation of application, deadline, decision); one-stop structures for residents and companies; an attractive civil service with fully digital HR processes and recruitment in 90 days rather than many months
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::ti: appointment at any citizens’ office (Bürgeramt) within 14 days; repeal outdated/contradictory rules; clearer Berlin Senate (Senat)–district task split; public portal with municipal-enterprise data and free access to contracts from €100,000; mobile citizens’ office (Bürgeramt) units
cellSummaries.governance-and-administrative-reform::oe: E-government and priority improvements to equipment so the administration becomes faster and more efficient; full transparency of administrative actions and support for the “Berlin Transparency Act” initiative
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::cdu: BärGPT, E-Health, digital applications for WBS and housing benefit
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::spd: The rent-price check app and a rent and housing register; a renewed digital agency and “digitalization guides” in the districts, AI in building authorities, Governance Technology for public services, and AI and Open Data as a dedicated economic cluster
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::gruene: digitalization law (Digitalgesetz); “Public Money, Public Code”—contracts only for open source; Open Data, Berlin-App, a digital citizens’ office (Bürgeramt) with video consultations and real-time application status, and digital sovereignty instead of dependence on the US and China
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::linke: prioritize Open Source and digital sovereignty in public procurement; strengthen the data-protection commissioner’s rights and resources and review admin database access for discrimination; strict rules against non-consensual sexualized deepfakes; stronger privacy oversight of police data holdings
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::fdp: AI for a freer, working city: digital office assistants and KI translation of authority texts into plain language; AI appointment booking with real-time slots and a digital waitlist; transparent, controllable AI in administration; Berlin as a model region for digital health (telemedicine, apps) with strong hospital cybersecurity
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::afd: Strategic digitalization for quality of life and to strengthen Berlin as a technology hub; data protection and privacy are “not negotiable”—against providers searching for “politically inconvenient” content; cooperation with private business and a federal digitalization strategy
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::bsw: Digitalization as a “learning tool, not a substitute for education”: digital skills across all subjects, but with critical reflection and ethics; smartphones and tablets out of primary school; broader use of AI in the civil service
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::volt: once-only data, interoperable systems and fully digital services; Public Money/Public Code for publicly funded software; pilot then roll out GovTech citywide; chamber-defined minimum standards so AI is usable and safe for small firms; open data as a base for new services; investigative software from European providers
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::tierschutz: prefer Open Source, fund ITDZ, Public Money/Public Code, and reuse proven solutions from other Länder; data centers feed waste heat into the heating network; continue fiber rollout and restore Free Wifi Berlin; AI in admin/police/justice only under human oversight, algorithmic transparency, no Social Scoring
cellSummaries.digitalization-data-ai::oedp: use E-Governing and prioritize equipment; more Open Source in municipal IT for flexibility and less vendor lock-in; lower mobile-radio limit to 100 μW/m² and designate white zones for electrosensitive people
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::cdu: The SOZIALES BERLIN platform as a single point of access to assistance
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::spd: city-wide anti-poverty strategy; push collectively bargained pay toward ~80% coverage; cap care co-payments and fair pay in care
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::gruene: Housing First, a protected housing-market segment and a municipal housing-search service, a fund for people with energy debt, and stronger social housing services
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::linke: 20 neighborhood canteens (€10 million per year), heating-cost fund, and free education from Kita through university
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::fdp: Subject-based rather than object-based support: people in need receive sufficient housing benefit to rent on the market; against poverty in old age through education, savings, and one’s own pension—“advancement through achievement, not complete state support”
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::afd: Priority for long-term residents and “high contributors” in the allocation of municipal housing; home ownership as protection against poverty in old age; “poverty immigration” described as a burden on social systems; outpatient family support instead of expanding authorities
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::bsw: A minimum wage of €15 per hour and pensions up to €2,000 tax-free; a dedicated section on “combating poverty”—one in four children lives in a household receiving basic benefits; the city again pays Mieterverein dues for social-benefit recipients
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::volt: Routes out of structural unemployment: modular retraining and socially useful employment at the minimum wage where the market does not provide needed work; BuT-Pass for children from low-income families and “Berlin Gets Moving”; meeting places against loneliness—multigenerational cafés and neighborhood centers
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::tierschut: Increase Regelbedarf, restore Berlin-Pass, and make social tickets non-discriminatory; test universal basic income; more staff in social-service authorities, citywide street social work with multiyear rather than project funding, and mobile Kiez teams; free menstrual hygiene products in schools, universities, and public authorities; accessibility and vegan meals in public institutions; a commissioner for combating loneliness
cellSummaries.social-affairs-poverty-income::oedp: parenting wage independent of income; do not count child benefit against citizens’ benefit (Bürgergeld); no profit orientation in childcare and elderly care
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::cdu: A separate chapter, “Culture and media”: Jugendclubs as meeting places and spaces for democratic education with mandatory safeguarding concepts; a mandatory strategy for major cultural and sporting events and an Olympic bid; S-Bahn arches for culture and crafts; support against antisemitism in culture (OpenArtsHub); culture of remembrance and memorial work
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::spd: For the first time, a support program for club venues (club-venue funding) and implementation of Berlin’s club strategy; against severe cuts to culture, reliable funding for district culture, libraries, music schools, galleries, and sociocultural venues; continued support for games plus new support for e-sports
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::gruene: A separate chapter on protecting Berlin’s club culture, “Berlin is culture,” independent media and press
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::linke: protect club culture: commercial rent cap, venue funding and noise protection
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::fdp: A separate chapter, “In step with the times—strengthen club culture”: include club venues in urban planning and secure them long-term, apply the Agent of Change principle, create a single contact point for the club scene in districts and the Berlin Senate (Senat), simplify and speed up approvals, include clubs in the tourism strategy; a new building for the ZLB central library
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::afd: A chapter on “Art, culture, media, and remembrance policy”: preserving “cultural heritage” is the first task; funding museums and archives takes priority over supporting cultural practitioners themselves; support “high culture” that cannot survive on the market; require culture funding (Kulturförderung) not to fund projects opposed to the free democratic order or conducive to antisemitism; more money from the federal Hauptstadtkulturfonds
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::bsw: A state Cultural Funding Act modeled on Lower Saxony, Saxony, and Saxony-Anhalt—binding cooperation structures, transparency, and predictability; reverse radical cuts to the culture budget; allocate all overnight-tax revenue to culture, as in Hamburg, Cologne, and Erfurt; a Kulturpass (culture pass) for teenagers from low-income families
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::volt: Secure culture for the long term: reliable structural funding in the Land and all districts instead of short-term project money; a binding cultural development plan with civil-society participation; a strategy for EU funding and “guides” for districts; open vacant commercial space to culture without bureaucracy via a digital platform; recognize clubs as cultural venues and protect them through the Agent of Change principle (the party arriving later pays for sound insulation); support Open Airs, cultural education for all, culture of remembrance, and European exchange
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::tierschutz: Culture as a public good: long-term contractual core funding, including for small stages, clubs, and self-managed venues; put clubs on an equal legal footing with theaters and concert halls and protect them from displacement and strict noise rules; recognize music venues as serving the public good; restore free Museum Sunday; legalize Street Art and expand legal walls; open vacant municipal buildings to culture; ecological standards and vegan menus in cultural institutions; renovation instead of demolition; return unlawfully acquired cultural property
cellSummaries.culture-and-clubs::oedp: Culture in every district plus space for creative professionals and shared workshops; restore Museum Sunday (free admission to all museums on the first Sunday of the month); legal certainty for music schools and adult education centers following the 2022 court ruling; plan venues and youth culture with support for interim use
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::cdu: school sport with a performance focus; swimming skills; first floating football pitch (not stadium) in Rummelsburger Bucht with a feasibility study
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::spd: invest in municipal pools: standardized swimming halls and climate-friendly renovation; free swimming for clubs, Kitas and schools; extend Landessportbund support agreement beyond 2029
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::gruene: Sports for all: inclusive and climate-neutral infrastructure, accessibility, universal swimming instruction, and climate-neutral sporting events
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::linke: Daily physical activity in all schools: renovation and construction of sports facilities plus training for physical-education teachers; swimming lessons for everyone within a reasonable timeframe, with the city reimbursing districts for “swimming buses” and free pool admission for children; All-Gender changing rooms and separate cubicles, digital and transparent allocation of sports facilities, and stronger district sports offices
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::fdp: A bid for the 2036 (or 2040) Olympic and Paralympic Games, modernizing existing facilities and building new ones only where necessary for sport; preserve the Olympic training-center sites and create “Sports City Berlin-Hohenschönhausen”; facility repairs by users with financial predictability and an emphasis on accessibility; nothing in the program about swimming lessons or pools
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::afd: Enshrine the right to transport to swimming lessons (“swimming bus”) in school law and move swimming from grade 3 to grade 2—“every child should learn to swim”; criticism of closed pools, long journeys, and waiting lists at swimming clubs; give greater attention to accessibility for people with disabilities when building and renovating sports facilities, and deliver an inclusive Jahn-Sportpark without cuts; strict rules against violence in amateur football and outdoor pools, an “achievement orientation,” and genuine Landesjugendspiele
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::bsw: “Sports for all,” prioritizing grassroots sport over elite sport and mega-events: restore sports infrastructure (need: €410 million versus €24 million per year), support ordinary clubs where thousands of children are waiting for a place, without fees or commercialization; dedicated support for women’s and girls’ sport, older people’s sport, and integration projects; ✗ an Olympic bid at the expense of grassroots sport and “over the heads of the population”
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::volt: Make better use of the city’s roughly 1,200 sports facilities: open schoolyards, halls, parks, and green spaces after classes, on weekends, and during holidays; transparent online booking for clubs and initiatives; at least one accessible, inclusive offering in each district (DIN 18040 standards, DOSB and DBS guidelines), protected hours for FLINTA groups; cheaper pool use, support for clubs working with migrants, more movement in Kita and schools; “Integration durch Sport” and the “Berlin Gets Moving” portal
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::tierschutz: Sport as a place for meeting and participation for everyone, regardless of gender, age, origin, or disability: accessibility in all districts and a goal of at least one fully inclusive sports facility per district; develop Jahn-Sportpark into an inclusive complex, including discussion of renaming; support programs such as “Sport im Park” and clubs opposing extremism; every child should learn to swim, with sufficient courses, pool capacity, and cooperation; free pool admission for children under 18 from single-parent families; ✗ Berlin Olympic bid; recognize E-Sport as serving the public good
cellSummaries.sports-and-swimming::oedp: Grassroots sport with district projects and swimming lessons for children and teenagers, expansion of sports facilities with an emphasis on inclusion, and barrier-free access to all public buildings and transport
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::cdu: Conversely, simplification: review and reduce the “confusing web” of participation structures, commissioners, and councils to improve administrative efficiency; a “digital twin” of the city as a participation platform with 3D visualization of projects; support children’s and youth parliaments; use video surveillance to highlight queerphobic crimes
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::spd: Develop the “Mein Berlin” participation platform, hold local dialogues with Berlin Senate (Senat) members and early information meetings on construction projects, and preserve district citizen-participation offices; intersectional equality policy as a cross-cutting task in all laws and gender-responsive budgeting in the Land budget; a dedicated strategy against online hate, including antisemitism, racism, sexism, and queerphobia; queer-sensitive medicine
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::gruene: Structural equality, protection from discrimination, queer safety, inclusion, East German perspectives, action against right-wing extremism, and “Berlin—a child-friendly city” with children’s rights to vote and submit motions
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::linke: voting rights for people without German citizenship after at least five years’ residence; strengthen participation councils; “School against the Right” (anti-far-right education in schools)
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::fdp: citizen participation as a condition for all transport planning (support for the initiative “against bollards and Kiezblocks”); support queer networks in state-owned enterprises, authorities, and businesses—“Berlin should be a place where queer people are safe, visible, and self-determined”; strengthen senior citizens’ representative bodies and abolish the State Seniors’ Advisory Council
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::afd: “Equality instead of equalizing outcomes”: reduce the institution of equality and anti-discrimination commissioners and reject “trans ideology”; more direct democracy through direct election of the mayor and a “Volkseinwand” against “bad laws”
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::bsw: More direct democracy: laws adopted by referendum can be changed only by another vote (example: development at the edge of Tempelhofer Feld); the Berlin Senate (Senat) and parliament can themselves submit important questions to a vote (example: an Olympic bid); a peace agenda opposing rearmament and conscription
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::volt: Embed participation in the system: regular randomly selected citizens’ assemblies reflecting the city’s diversity, with politicians and the administration required to respond publicly to their recommendations; mandatory participatory budgets in the districts and at Land level, and genuine residents’ budgets with guaranteed implementation (Paris example: around 5 percent of the investment budget); optional referendum: if parliament changes a law adopted by referendum, only 2.5 percent of voters are needed to trigger a new popular vote; voting rights for EU citizens and participation by international Berliners without German passports in citizens’ assemblies; a Transparency Act requiring publication of key documents such as expert opinions, Senate decisions and contracts; a Land queer-safety strategy
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::tiersc: Lower the thresholds for direct democracy: quorums, online signature collection, and lowering the threshold for resident petitions from 1,000 to 200; put in place the referendums “Expropriate Deutsche Wohnen & Co.,” “Berlin climate-neutral by 2030,” Tempelhofer Feld, “car-free Berlin,” and “ad-free Berlin”; voting rights for everyone who has lived in Berlin for at least three years, lower the voting age to 14 in the districts, abolish the Neutrality Act (ban on religious symbols for many public servants); better protection for queer people and greater accessibility
cellSummaries.democracy-participation-equality::oedp: Mandatory local referendums at district and Land levels, citizens’ assemblies for neighborhood and district decisions with binding rules for implementing proposals, a genuine Transparency Act without loopholes, voting from age 16 and voting rights for EU citizens in parliamentary elections, a ban on party donations from companies and interest groups; civic service as a form of participation
cellSummaries.women-s-rights-and-prevention-of-domesti: state action plan to implement the Istanbul Convention; more shelter places including a 10th women’s shelter; prevention and perpetrator measures (incl. electronic monitoring)

gender equality as a cross-cutting task including gender budgeting; parity law for real equality; implement the Istanbul Convention; expand women’s shelters and protection; systematic police risk analyses; better protection from femicide; violence-prevention act and independent police/citizen commissioners

two new women’s shelters plus more second-stage housing; implement the Violence Assistance Act and Istanbul Convention; Spanish-model police procedures for domestic violence; “Who hits, leaves”; digital-violence counseling and perpetrator work

defend and expand women’s shelters, counseling and girls’ projects with tariff pay; implement the Istanbul Convention and Violence Assistance Act; state coordination office; mandatory perpetrator courses; school education against sexism and domestic violence

implement Istanbul Convention pillars; expand women’s-shelter / refuge places and the violence-protection outpatient clinic (forensic documentation of injuries); funded prevention centers + perpetrator work; STEM equality, pregnancy-conflict counseling, equal pay and public-service leadership parity

Significant focus on domestic violence: the Spanish model—an electronic ankle monitor when a court imposes a restraining order and a victim notification system; expansion of the women’s shelter network and multilingual information about assistance

Electronic ankle monitors for perpetrators of domestic violence, at least 330 additional places in women’s shelters to fulfill the Istanbul Convention, and digital sexualized violence as a distinct form of violence; the Barnahus model for children and British interagency risk teams

Strong section: women’s shelters at the level required by the Istanbul Convention, training for police, justice, and authorities on hate speech, stalking, and femicide, low-threshold online counseling, and more psychosocial assistance; free menstrual hygiene products in schools, universities, and public authorities
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::cdu: affirms same-sex relationships as part of Berlin’s Heimat (sense of home/belonging); supports World Pride / InterPride bids; also expands video surveillance against queerphobic crime
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::spd: implement and fund LGBTIQ+ action plan (LSBTIQ+-Aktionsplan) 2023; queer affairs commissioners (Queerbeauftragte) in all districts; Rainbow Network (Regenbogennetzwerk); strategy against online hate including queerphobia; queer-sensitive medicine
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::gruene: Queere Sicherheit (queer safety): at least one queer center/youth or family place per district; queer affairs commissioners (Queerbeauftragte) in all districts with a legal basis; Queer-Mainstreaming; equal access to health, housing and work
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::linke: Queer policy chapter: Rainbow Capital (Berlin as an LGBTQ+ haven) with a queer advisory board; fight queer poverty and housing discrimination; expand LGBTQ+ refugee shelters and queer housing for older people; protect queer bars, clubs and centers
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::fdp: Support queer networks in state-owned enterprises, authorities, and businesses: Berlin as a place where queer people are safe, visible, and self-determined
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::afd: “Equality instead of equalizing outcomes,” reduction of equality and anti-discrimination commissioners, and rejection of “trans ideology”
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::bsw: scrap the state “acceptance of sexual and gender diversity” contact point as failed; redirect funds to projects against homophobic violence
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::volt: A Land queer-safety strategy, regional centers assisting victims of extremist, racist, and anti-queer violence, and psychological and legal assistance
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::tierschutz: Protection for queer people, abolition of the Neutrality Act (ban on religious symbols for many public servants), and anti-discrimination; independent police complaints and measures against discriminatory practices
cellSummaries.queer-and-lgbtq-issues::oedp: A Berlin based on solidarity, inclusion, and openness to the world, without discrimination based on lifestyle or beliefs
cellSummaries.elections-second-vote-and-5-percent-thre: instead, parity-based electoral reform and parity in the party’s own structures, the Berlin Senate (Senat), and municipal enterprises

voting from age 16 has been achieved, and the next step is to lower the voting age further and give voting rights to everyone whose center of life is in Berlin, regardless of citizenship (almost one million people are excluded from elections)
